bacr_question_full: Brand Analytics, to quantify the impact of a company’s brand on marketing and company performance

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Simple reporting of brand metrics – largely conducted by 3rd party agencies. Little analysis to link specific activity with business outcomes.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Growing range of brand effectiveness metrics – integrating internal and external measures to report on aggregate effectiveness of brand building activities
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Growing range of brand effectiveness metrics – integrating internal and external measures to report on effectiveness of brand building activities – with ability to isolate the impact of specific advertising and direct marketing activities
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Large range of brand effectiveness metrics – integrating internal and external measures to report on effectiveness of brand building activities – with ability to isolate the impact of specific activities. Analytics used to drive a growing number of activities such as calendar planning, product development, pricing and media buying.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Comprehensive range of brand effectiveness metrics – integrating internal and external measures to report on effectiveness of brand building activities – with ability to isolate the impact of specific activities. Analytics used to drive a large number of activities such as calendar planning, product development and media buying. Sophisticated forecasting and simulation models enables optimisation of the media mix and marketing budget. Measures of Brand Equity calculated, tracked and reported,

bacr_question_full: Research New Product Development Opportunities, to leverage external market research, trends and internal product usage data to support product and packaging design and specifications

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Little to no investment in researching new product ideas. Decisions made based on past experience and/or personal preferences. Generally repeat what worked last year and plan inventory based on last year’s product usage and sales statistics plus expected growth. Performance depends on the capabilities of individuals or teams and varies with their innate skills, knowledge, and motivations.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Understanding of the need to efficiently manage the product development lifecycle and the limitation of being reactive to declining product revenue. Utilize surveys and focus groups to understand market direction and identify product categories. Most new product introductions are limited to evolutionary changes.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: A standard process for developing new products is documented. This process can be characterized as including inputs, standards and procedures for performing the work, metrics for verification, and other standard outputs. Emerging use of analytic techniques, such as sentiment analysis, to better understand customer needs and expectations with the use of customer and usage data
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Established metrics for product development processes. The development process is predictable because the process is measured and operates within measurable limits. Utilize analytic techniques, such as sentiment analysis, to better understand customer needs and expectations systematically using customer and usage data
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: The entire organization is focused on continuous process improvement characterized by an agile new product development methodology. Able to predict emerging trends and gain first mover advantage. Advanced predictive analytics incorporated into methodology.

bacr_question_full: Predict Business Impact (Discovery), which is the prediction of product launce impact on resources, assets and market adoption, to support business case and investment justification

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: No change or adaptation of internal resources. Sales volumes are anticipated by simply extrapolating trends based on previous launches.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Increased readiness of internal resources based on forecasted sales volumes. Expected product uptake based on historical patterns of relevant and similar products as well as market trends, and competitive analysis
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Internal resource readiness planned based on expected product uptake, where cannibalisation analysis is added, as well as expected product related customer experience. This is obtained by things like text and sentiment analysis from digital channels, either from historical similar product launches or from current pre-announcements.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Resource planning based on additional insight of product launch impact on total product portfolio. Product affinity analysis can be added to support this.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Proactive communication with targeted customers who are predicted to influence product uptake both from a sales and customer experience perspective.  As an example this can in a Telco be achieved by SNA (Social Network Analysis) in combination with other analytical techniques.

bacr_question_full: Develop and Test Product Prototypes, including testing and evaluating alternative product specifications and features, including AB testing, and product preview statistics

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Operationalizing new multi-genre and open source analytics  leveraging the discovery platform of  several wireless and wire line products,  content viewership data, multichannel  data and other customer behavioral data. This is considered to be emerging analytics that all telecommunications companies want to execute and Teradata is best suited to help deliver this success.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Developing new multi-genre analytics and open source analytics  leveraging the discovery platform of  several wireless and wire line products,  content viewership data, multichannel data and other customer behavioral data..
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Storing content viewership data with wireless / wire line data in one discovery platform and/or data schema enables rapid deployment of analytics. Additionally, incorporating multichannel and other customer behavioral data will provide an advanced data repository which can accommodate multi-structured data and support multi-genre analytics. Single platform for integrated data enables repeatable analytics.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Traditional wireless and wire line data, including viewership data, can be integrated in one platform and analyzed to yield insight into segmentation of customers and products. Continued advanced analytics of online / app viewership data can enable telecommunication companies to make superior content delivery offerings with compelling packages.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: For telecommunications companies to remain relevant, they will need to create compelling content offerings which integrate and evolve traditional home solutions and wireless innovation.

bacr_question_full: Source Products and Develop Contracts, including managing costs, risks, quality, service levels and performance of vendors that supply products or raw materials

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Manual sharing and analysis of demand data and forecasts via spread sheets. Vendor purchasing data includes limited historical data available.  Raw materials data is siloed or non-existent.  Product costs are not known; estimates are used to calculate final (LLC) costs.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Development of a sales portal to share demand data with suppliers. Manual reporting to provide integrated view of sales, costs, margin, and service levels across vendors/suppliers. More formal process of collating sales and cost data to support vendor negotiations.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Optimize vendor selection and purchase agreement/buying negotiations. Collaborative Forecasting for long range product revenue goals. Quarterly review includes vendor compliance analysis and is used to craft future contracts by vendor.  Integrated sales, costs and inventory data available.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Clear cost of sales structure in place – Detailed product profitability analysis and well defined pricing structure. Consistent cost calculation methods across the enterprise and across vendors. Timely and on-demand  vendor and product  performance analysis with a granularity on the product level in an automated exception driven process – good understanding of vendor profitability - well defined pricing guidance – Cost optimization initiatives  in place lacking prioritization  - Enhanced procurement decisions limited to major products . Combination of ERP and non ERP data.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Close collaboration between partners to address joint challenges and improve costs, efficiencies and service. Portals to provide integrated visibility into the status of WIP or finished products across all production and transportation vendors.

bacr_question_short: Plan Product Investments to Support Go-to-Market Strategy
bacr_question_full: Plan Product Investments to Support Go-to-Market Strategy, including holistic evaluation and determination of appropriate initial resource, capital and infrastructural investment for product launch

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Basic forecasting and allocation practices. No enterprise view of inventory ownership. Go-to-market processes and cycle for each functional unit is lengthy, manual and non-aligned. Siloed processes in place but no cross-function or business cooperation. Promotional inventory based on historical trends. Little variability in assortments
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Improved cross-functional communications during planning process. Basic alignment of some functions and channels. Leverage predictive forecasting practices/ tools  for basic items. New product forecast done via manual historical tracking of similar products/ services. Actual versus Plan reporting to manage performance and adjust future plans. Financial plans and drivers are reconciled to ensure direction and strategy.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Cross-function flows still manual but using electronic means. Close alignment among channels and functions, with high level cross-functional cooperation, but on a project-by-project basis. Enterprise inventory visibility enabled. Seasonal forecasting practiced. Automated adjustment of product and location service levels based on product lifecycle stage. Assign products to branch clusters using profile-based attributes such as demographics/ lifestyle, financial profile and perception. Product/ service continuum planning to enable improved take-up rates. Competitor product suite  and pricing tracked. Leverage elasticity models for product campaign and promo inventory management
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Automation of cross-function approvals. Extensive cooperation, with integration between most functions. SLAs in place for fulfillment and delivery. average demand forecasting practices and tools for multiple product/ service suite. “Buy from anywhere, fulfill from  anywhere” capability enabled.  Automated fulfillment  via  parameters and rules. Full automation of new product introduction and history. Product suite optimized for key customer segments. Rationalization of vendors and product suite based on margin and profitability. analyze product/service continuum gaps. Integrate campaign planning, marketing and inventory planning. Robust calculation of campaign ROI
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Full automation of all workflow driven processes from campaign design to final approvals. Full organizational alignment and integration across channels, functions and business units. Detailed SLAs for fulfillment coupled with transformed culture of collaboration. End to end product management and complete supply chain visibility. “What if” analytics well entrenched.  Unified pricing, campaign and Product suite modeling. Consider near real time competitor product proposition and pricing analytics. Incorporate customer segment definitions into assortment (range) planning process to support customer-centric merchandising across all channels. Track performance of product campaigns in near real time

bacr_question_full: Improve Product Onboarding, including optimizing the process of onboarding new products and predicting the impact on business performance and customer behaviour

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Product centric approach to product launch.  New products are measured based on the single objective of unit sales.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Beginning to monitor cross channel implications and impact on other products. Considers market impact and customer satisfaction. Reactive response to infrastructure issues (e.g. call center, supply chain and operations) are modeled and shared functionally.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Reactive cross channel analysis, including impact of cannibalization.  Beginning to conduct basic analysis on customer impact.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Proactively conducting basic analysis on customer and infrastructure impact based on results from similarly launched items.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: In advance of a product launch, predicting the impact on the customer and the business. This includes external  feedback (including social input) to identify and react to product launch issues.  Also developed a continuous feedback loop to improve product specifications and launch processes for future enhancements.

bacr_question_full: Analyzing Competitive Pricing, including collection and analysis of competitive pprices to determine need to reset prcies of key products, categories, and services based upon pricing strategy.  Understand and simulate the impact of price adjustments to sales and profits

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Pricing optimizing for revenue maximization based on comparison of competitor prices on the market
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Pricing optimization  toward competitors on improved granularity of local market position, reactive to recognized competitive price position changes
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Competitive price considering not only competiton prices but substitute produc prices. Service usage patterns recognized to match competitve pricing schemes
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Competitve pricing optimizing for driving future service usage habits/purchasing habits to maximize revenues  on deep granularity market view. Predictive analytics supports modeling future usage habit pattern insights for pricing
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Pricing optimized by proactive actions based on competitor move prediction in a deep granularized market view, providing right time response to competitive pricing changes. Predictive analytics on expected competitor pricing moves.

bacr_question_full: Adjust Product Lifecycle Pricing, which is the ability to model and proactively set/adjust prices to maximize profit during all life stages of a product

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Prices points are determined based on established markdown cadence and rules by channel.  Price points set based on rules within operational system or basic buyer formulae.  No formal pricing analytics or pricing organization. Incorporate wallet, discount and loyalty redemption into pricing.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Companies implement a pricing/markdown optimization tool.  Tool may be outsourced or in-house.  Tool is likely not comprehensive and may only addresses limited aspect of pricing strategy, typically clearance.  Users may distrust pricing recommendations, with frequent overrides being the norm.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Beginning to establish organization to manage statistics to drive price strategy.  Focus is on maximizing  profitability.  Begin to operationalize seasonal variability of pricing by location and explore elasticity of demand for promotional events. Zone and store level pricing is possible.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Experienced pricing team exist that are capable of building new models. Customer data  is incorporated into pricing decisions.  Pricing recommendations are understood and accepted by business users.  Buy Plans and Sales Forecasts are regularly evaluated via scenario planning.  Exploration of channel-driven pricing
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Companies can set price at location or channel level.  Capable of managing dynamic prices in near real time.   Personalized prices based on individual customers is possible, incorporating wallet, discount and loyalty redemption into pricing.   Predictive analytics are consistently used to anticipate performance and to  plan advantageous buys.

bacr_question_full: Manage Dynamic Pricing, reactively adjusting prices based on resource availabilty to shape demand and manage yeild in right/near-real time.  Prices may fluctuate based on time of day, space and usage amongst other events

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Pricing scheme update monthly /weekly based on stock  and sales target information (internal information)
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Pricing scheme updated daily based on stock, sales target and customer information (internal information, but extended range of internal data domains)
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Pricing scheme updates  (daily) are driven by business rules representing product strategy, customer strategy, stock clearance rules etc. Business rules representing internal  business events, business trends and predictions (such as estimated sales).
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating:
Actual and relevant pricing available at the right time for customer interaction, applying one or two  pricing schemes across the entire product portfolio using actual values of product attributes to calculate individual  price (or individual discount)  for the purchase event. Selected attributes may fall into different categories such as:
Seasonality, order lead time, Time of day
Location of customer/ POS
available stock, strategic product categorization, end-of-life, bridge products  etc
Customer Loyalty scheme etc
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Pricing business rules evaluated/prioritzed across more dynamic price options at the right time for the purchase transaction. Different product assortments may apply different dynamic pricing rule priorization at the time of purchase transaction.

bacr_question_short: Plan and Manage Promotional Items / Offers
bacr_question_full: Plan and Manage Promotional Items / Offers, involving modeling of promotional offets (prices, bundles etc.) to predict impact on sales to support the promotions planning process

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Promotional items are selected based upon last year, same event history.  Manually account for calendar and event shifts in plan. Promotional prices are established based on buyer designated price points . Many promotional items are selected based on vendor funding or market development funds available
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Leverage lift and UPT analytics of historical events for planning. Analyze historical basket size and affinity item combinations during promotions  to understand variances in geography or channel and to improve future promotions. Reference historical competitor promotions (often collected manually or in excel)
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Forecast promotion outcome for the enterprise.   Perform price elasticity modeling to anticipate demand and inventory requirements for promoted items.   Include historical halo and cannibalization analytics .  Proactively address competitor pricing strategy, based on history.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Forecast promotional outcomes by location. Evaluate featured-item candidates  for promotions  to predict impact on featured and companion items. Evaluate candidate  items based on promotional forecast PLUS the ability to draw other items into the  basket.  Identify items which sell together to create promotional bundles.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Mine ecommerce data to track “first in the basket”  as part of the promotional strategy. Plan personalized promotions for specific customers based on behavior. Automate tracking and storing of competitive item information for future reference.

bacr_question_full: Measure Promotional Effectiveness, tracking and assessing the impact of a promotion on sales of the promoted product, categories, affinity products and customer behaviour

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Analysis of promoted item performance is conducted after the event.   Users rely on merchandise sales reports and pre-during-post event analysis for the weeks in which the event occurred.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Perform little in-promotion analysis; most analysis is done after the event.   Manual tracking of competitor promotions. Track average transaction size and UPT by geography or channel to understand influence of Promotions.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Promotion performance analysis is geared toward specific dates on which the promotion occurred (not bound by whole week). Daily analysis of  basket size and affinity item combinations during promotions  to understand variances in geography or channel. Adjust promotions in-flight. Analyze roles of products within the assortment.  Identify “driver” and “companion” items with in the assortment to maximize overall profitability of events.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Track actual  lift by event by location. Analyze promoted item performance intra- day. Measure attachment rates  and evaluate promotional  investments in cherry picked items (items which do not drive the sale of any other items). Dashboards and exception reports are used to highlight variances and trends outside the norm / plan.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Optimize promo space to maximize traffic and volume, by location. Track performance of promoted items in near real time. Change promotion or promotional pricing for different day parts. Execute on personalized promotions for specific customers based on behavior. Alert and respond to competitive price moves in comparable items or key categories.

bacr_question_full: Optimize Product Placement, looking at how products are co-located either in-store or on the web page and how this impacts on driving customer behaviour and shopping missions.

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Planograms for different categories planned in isolation, no consideration of product affinities across categories or product groups. Promotion product placement driven by potential uplifts or supplier funding to capture best locations (eg Gondola ends). Standard planograms across all stores or regions/formats
maturity_descriptors.2_developing:
Product placement and co-location based upon “obvious” product associations.
Standard planograms across all stores or regions/formats
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing:
Cross category product affinities  used to select product placement and adjacencies in store and on web pages. Needs a more holistic approach to product placement considering cross category affinities. 
Basic store clustering  based on demographics, size etc. used to drive product placement.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating:
Shopping mission analysis to understand key drivers of shopping mission and gateway products which drive  larger shopping missions, combining missions. Using this insight to drive product placement and adjacencies.
Store clustering based on shopping behavior  to drive cluster specific product placement.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Analyzing Customer movements in store by tracking their mobile phones through the store using beacons to identify hot and cold spots. Linking Customer movements to baskets to determine optimum layouts to drive larger baskets. Using Customer product affinities to select online product placement and co-location.

bacr_question_full: Optimize Micro and Macro Space, analyzing performnce to determine space allocations for cateogires (macro) and  individual products (micro) to optimize sales densities (per square meter/foot), revenue and margin

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Manual data collection and spreadsheet data manipulation to prepare data for planogramming process. Typically performed at chain level .
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Macro (Category) and Micro (product) space allocations planned in isolation, not considering cross category influences or Customer behaviors/shopping missions. Typically generated at chain level based on store formats and available space. Sales densities of categories and products not actively measured
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Space allocation consider product affinities to promote specific baskets and Customer behaviors. Typically generated at chain level based on store formats and available space. Sales densities of categories and products seen as a critical KPI for store sales performance comparisons
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Space allocations consider local customer behaviors and shopping missions. Typically stores are clustered by Customer behaviors /shopping missions
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Dynamic space flexing to consider changes in shopping behaviors during the week and different shopping behaviors at weekend (e.g. smaller missions through the week, larger missions at weekend).

bacr_question_short: Optimize Assortments / Ranges or Product Mix
bacr_question_full: Optimize Assortments / Ranges or Product Mix, including building a product assortment / product mix by channel or location to reflect customer shopping behaviours

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Typically assortment proliferates as new products are introduced without removing existing products, driving low sales densities due to too many slow moving product. Ranging decisions based on product sales performance.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Centralised assortments based on store demographics formats and price bands. Ranging decisions based on product sales performance.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Store cluster assortments optimized using product affinities, Ranging decisions based on basket analysis , to understand which products are important to which basket types.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Assortment based on understanding of Customer behaviors and shopping missions in individual stores. Stores clustered based on like behaviors. Ranging decisions made with Customer behavior and shopping missions in mind. Product affinities from on-line transactions used to inform store ranging decisions
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: More localized assortments based on individual stores Customer behaviors and shopping missions (typically a core cluster range, with a proportion “localized” to individual stores. Product affinities from on-line transactions used to inform store ranging decisions. Able to incorporate local traffic and population data from prospective customer intelligence into range decisions.

bacr_question_full: Support Product Clearance, to dispose of excess or aged inventory to optimise sell through, markdowns and margins by modeling reduced prices and best locations in which to liquidate a product by an end date

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Excess inventory distributed to locations based on their size and sales, No consideration of their previous sales performance of the product or how much stock they already have
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Excess inventory allocated to locations based on their size and their previous sales of the products – no consideration of existing stockholding
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Excess inventory allocated to locations based on their size, their previous sales of the products and existing stockholding
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Excess inventory distributed to locations based on each locations forecasted sales and current inventory, balanced to give each location the same inventory cover so clearance is synchronized across all locations
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Leading organizations will have identified the potential issue of excess inventory before it occurs by using future inventory projections highlighting potential excess stock situations giving them the opportunity to circumvent the excess inventory – reduced orders, order delay, advertising etc.

bacr_question_short: Determine Product Migration is the identification and priori
bacr_question_full: Determine Product Migration is the identification and prioritization of products to be decommissioned and migrated to selected new products, optimizing customer value and business benefits

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Determine products for decommissioning based on number of customers owning the product or general sales volumes. Migrate to products based on current new product sales targets. Little or no understanding of customer and business impact
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Determine products for decommissioning based on number of customers owning the product or general sales volumes, as well as some insight on product utilization. Migrate to products based on current new product sales targets and product attributes to meet customer utilization needs. Basic understanding of customer and business impact
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Basic application of analytical techniques to determine products for decommissioning as well as recommended new product, based on product utilization and product portfolio ownerships. Initial understanding of costs associated with the product.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Application of analytical techniques to determine products for decommissioning as well as recommended new product, based on customer value , customer satisfaction and customer behavior. Significant understanding of costs and complexity associated with the product. Good understanding of customer and business impact.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Application of advanced analytical techniques to determine products for decommissioning as well as recommended new product, based on extensive customer insight and customer influential impact on customer base value.  Analytics also inform about timing of recommended migration. Full understanding of customer and business impact, including predicted indirect impact.

bacr_question_full: Optimize Reduce to Clear is the reduction of wastage and optimization of margin on perishable products that come to the end of their shelf life via intra-day analytics

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Manual checking of shelves to find products near end of shelf life. Manual consideration of  potential excess stock Undirected arbitrary local price reductions which dilute margin and sales revenue
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Manual checking of shelves to find products near end of life. Central price reduction recommendations, typically a set percentage discount. no consideration of levels of excess stock
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Manual checking of shelves to find products near end of life, Set guidelines of discounts for locations for follow depending on excess stock
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Central calculation of potential excess stock levels in each location, alerts to stores. Dynamic pricing calculations to  optimize sell through, margin and wastage
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Central calculation of potential excess stock levels in each location using hourly sales to pick up last minute opportunities, alerts to stores, Dynamic pricing calculations  and timing calculations using within day sales to  optimize sell through, margin and wastage

bacr_question_full: Support Product Recalls, to leverage customer purchase history to efficiently and proactively notify users of recalled products whilst optimizing costs and processes associated with them

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: No proactive response to product recalls.  Customers may hear about the recall  from public news sources, not from the manufacturer or seller. Identifying and factoring in new information (e.g. Engineering and Manufacturing) to understand/diagnose drivers of recalls and to monitor and track outstanding ones.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: POS data is mined to identify specific customers who purchased a recalled product.  Customers are proactively notified that a product that they purchased may have been affected by a product recall. Customer is responsible for checking model, lot or manufacturing dates to determine if their purchased product is affected. Recall notification takes weeks to process. Periodic use of new data types/streams (e.g. Engineering and Manufacturing) to better forecast recalls, understand/diagnose drivers of recalls and to monitor and track outstanding ones.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Monitor social site mentions of product to identify optimal platform on which to issue information and further updates on recall. Incorporate social media data with historical sales and web data  to capture changes in brand or product sentiment.  Leverage personalization to respond to changes. Leveraging analytics on all relevant, integrated data sets to forecast recalls, manage them from end-to-end, and more surgically identify specific products to recall from the field.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Manufacturers track lineage of products at all points in the production cycle.  Integrated traceability data helps to identify root cause and to respond quicker. Leverage detailed data to improve negotiations with suppliers to recoup recall costs.  Manufacturers can isolate defective components or defective lots, avoiding massive blanket recalls. Recalls are focused only on affected lots and the affected customers. Recall notifications take hours to process.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Quality Managers routinely scrape customer comments to identify issues, then  adjust quality parameters accordingly. Track variances  in historical patterns (such as returns) to foresee problems. Establish a temporary or permanent data exchange infrastructure to make affected customer data available  to manufacturers. Use of comprehensive and prescriptive analytical models that reduce recalls and associated costs  to industry –leading levels. Analytics used for management of recalls and to better inform product design and manufacturing processes.

bacr_question_full: Analyzing Market Basket and Affinity to leverage transaction level data to develop insight into customer behaviour, shopping missions and affinity

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Measure basic basket metrics such as basket size, revenue, and gross margin by location.  Incorporate affinity coefficients to understand driver and passenger items. Score and compare basket trips types by location across time. Identify key shopper missions by location.  Uncover regional variances and opportunities to improve assortments.   Compare location basket size and profitability to district or region to identify outliers.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Leverage affinity analytics to build bundles, promotions and select advertised items. Extend analytics to include real estate attributes such as location selling size, location format and type. Track impact of basket metrics when competitors move in or out of markets or before, during and after promotions. Requires promo data. Companies design and develop Executive Dashboard to track basket segments
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Compare composition of baskets across channels. Analyze baskets of items that have traits that are trending (ex: organic, imported, high brand recognition or hot trend), Evaluate driver items as candidates for private label development.  Leverage market research along with key traits of current driver items to influence design of items in the  product development pipeline.  Requires extended product trait data and product development data.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Tailor format and layout of store to unique shopper segments of each location. Analyze customer segments (based  on trip mission) and the allocation of space to each trip segment by location. Identify mis-alignment of space and assortments. Requires planogram and assortment data
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Analyze ecommerce baskets to understand motivations for buying, starting with what item was placed into the market basket first. Understand impact of promoting “basket starters”.  Adjust promotional strategies and tailor offers to customers during the visit accordingly.  Expand findings from ecommerce baskets to influence catalogue features, store layouts, end cap presentations, promotions and pricing.   Requires ecommerce transaction and cart detail.

bacr_question_full: Analyze cross-channel performance to support the identification of opportunities for product bundling, cross- or up-selling and product wraps

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Basic channels tracked. Channel data typically siloed with little or no integration of functional matrices. Inventory typically housed within different warehouses with no consistent tracking of product codes/ numbers. Little or no campaign tracking capability that allows for response tracking across products. Most channels owned by different business units are not coordinated. Little or no automation at any level
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Channel management is entirely ad hoc, cross-channel delivery for acquisition activities not available. Organization is focused on driving costs out of the channel processes and maximizing individual sales.  Detailed transactional and financial information is typically not available immediately. Multi channel coordination typically sporadic or non-existent, Cross-channel cooperation improving but manual
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Multi-channel delivery and performance tracking. Organization defines and creates standard metrics for enterprise analysis.  Scorecards are built integrating results across business functions including limited non-financial data. Sporadic levels of automation. Little understanding of customer’s channel preference and limited resource optimization. Some integration of results across business functions. Gradual improvement in product ID’s to enable easy tracking of inventory across acquiring channels and originating warehouses
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Data analytics used to manage channel performance. Delivery and utilization is consistent with pre-defined metrics and business triggers.  Financial data is integrated with non-financial data to provide comprehensive reporting and analytic capabilities. Multi channel integration between web and static channels (in- and out-bound), sales force automation applications used with tracking capabilities. Extensive business rules used to manage channel delivery. KPI’s covering sales, customer satisfaction, inventory levels  and operational efficiency are embedded
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Fully automated analytics used to track multiple products across multiple channels. Messages coordinated across all channels in a sequential, logical and consistent manner. Customer channel preferences are embedded in all product and service strategies. Extensive use of channel mix and capacity optimization techniques Contact strategy and acquisition activities adapted to customer preference based on logical channel rules. Common channel tracking enabling acquisition from one locality and returns through another  or seamless inventory fulfillment from multiple warehouses across different branch, brand or geographic location

bacr_question_full: Manage Open to Buy.  Manage forward financial plans at a product level, optimizing the sales potential by product class or sub-class and location whilst also reducing inventory excess through the timely purchase of new or replacement stock

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Open to buy calculation is managed at category or department level on a monthly basis.  May be manual or excel based worksheet.  Sales forecast are based loosely on trend data.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Leverage data-driven sales forecasting for more accurate open to buy estimates for some product lines.  Leverage sales contribution patterns to determine future sales and  inventory investments.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Leverage algorithms to create accurate sales forecasts and inventory plans based on time-phased order forecasts for all products lines for each class or subclass by week or month.   What if scenario planning is used to explore potential sales and optimum required inventory for trending categories.  May manage open to buy projections for key items or key classifications. Incorporate detailed planning for units and currency with open to buy analytics. , Analytics are used to justify adjustments to current and future plans.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Expand algorithms to create accurate sales forecasts and inventory plans based on time-phased order forecasts down to location level.  Very granular view of open to buy allowing imbalances of inventory across locations to be identified and addressed.  Algorithms/models are measured for accuracy and adjusted as needed.  Leverage “what if” modeling to explore scenarios based on potential sales, inventory orders, markdowns, budget etc.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Analytics are used to highlight trending products and potential gaps between planned and actual sales and inventory levels to identify opportunities to reallocate budget to maximize sales.  May incorporate alerts and operational dashboards to proactively respond to actual variances against planned open to buy.

bacr_question_full: Compare to Product Benchmarks by comparing a portfolio against an internal or external reference to identify gaps and potential enhancements

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Products and services are benchmarked against internal metrics with no formal mechanisms to identify feedback from the marketplace.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Ad-hoc collection of feedback from the marketplace to inform product design and change. Typically to solve known issues and dealing with daily or regular processes and tasks.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Proactive and continuous feedback on significant KPIs across the product and channel range.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Significant effort invested across the product lifecycle for tracking and managing KPIs with feedback actively considered and acted upon.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Primary mission of the business to achieve operational excellence with benchmarking taking a strategic role in driving business innovation. Numerous mechanisms to generate active feedback to improve products and services.

bacr_question_full: Manage Product Profitability, quantifying all product and services (P&S) revenue, cost and risks to calculate the true profitability over time

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Basic NPV profitability models built in Excel using summarized data calculated on an ad-hoc basis.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Basic Excel-based NPV models for key products/segments using summarised results from current/historic profit model.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Basic product-level NPV model for existing product holdings only.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Automated propensity models for some key products used to enhance product strategy with attrition models for existing product holdings, and propensity to buy models for new products.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading:
Full and automated future / lifetime value model for individual products which includes comprehensive coverage of:
Projected cash flows from existing product holdings.
Attrition models for existing product holdings.
Propensity to buy models for new products.
Behavioral usage models for non-contractual products.

bacr_question_short: Produce Behavioural Segmentations.  Determine and leverage i
bacr_question_full: Produce Behavioural Segmentations.  Determine and leverage insights or patterns derived from detailed data of customer's products and services usage to design and evolve products and promote pricing, range and promotions.

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Measure product consumption and usage of individual products pushed into the market to determine simple purchase and usage low-dimensional segments using some market research to understand customer needs but not infer them from data.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Mainly use of market and consumer survey techniques, and competitive information to design and evolve individual P&S with no deep consideration of broader consumer/customer behaviors and groups. Customise P&S according to simple consumption/usage segments and measure performance in those segments.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing:
Design some specific P&Ss and promotions for specific usage/consumption segments and customer/consumer segments.
Use of market and consumer survey techniques, competitive information and internal usage/consumption patterns and segments to design and evolve individual P&S. Measure performance on those segments.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Base existing product strategy and operation on customer centric analytics and segmentations that feed back into product design and lifecycle. Design P&Ss and promotions for specific usage/consumption segments and customer/consumer segments. Routinely go through existing data to detect new P&S opportunities.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Predict and influence customer consumption and usage behaviors based on high-dimensional customer behavioral segments and prediction of emerging segments to drive product strategy, design, evolution and lifecycle. Base existing product strategy and operation on customer centric analytics and segmentations that feed back into product design and lifecycle. Measure performance on existing customer segments

bacr_question_full: Predict Product/Service Retention, using analytics to predict products that are likely to support continued use by customers or to be dropped by customers

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Basic events and measures calculated for use in ad-hoc product retention activity.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Identification of different product retention/churn scenarios and key data correlating to produce retention models. Analytics used to drive the development of treatment strategies to address retention issues. Small number of retention campaigns run on monthly batch cycle.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Retention model calculates customer segmentation based on product utilization which is used for weekly proactive retention campaigns. Single company understanding of product churn level definitions. Product affinity feeds into retention model.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Product or service revenue retention campaigns executed on a daily basis using lifecycle knowledge including decline in usage, decline in product holding or reduced activity. Social network analysis (SNA) feeds influential relationships into retention model.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Streamline results into company strategy and processes automatically or make decisions to change business process based on insights. Cross channel Next Best Action (NBA) based on complex churn-value analytics running automatically driven by context and real-time triggers.

bacr_question_full: Support Contract Management, to monitor performance in-season against contract terms

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Little or no follow up to track collection of vendor monies associated with contract terms.  Focused on using commercial terms to reduce cost of goods without consideration of supply chain costs
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Development of ad hoc reports to track actual performance vs. contract terms.   Manual integration of contract terms required. Little comparative analysis  across vendors or across departments.  Beginning to formalize a process of collating sales and cost data to support vendor negotiations.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Vendor commercials consider impacts of supply chain costs and efficiencies. Quarterly review of key vendor performance statistics includes a review of negotiated terms and actual performance. Integrated sales, costs and inventory data available, but manual integration of contract terms is required for analysis
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Automated and timely reporting of contract term violations and their impacts. Timely and on demand vendor and product  performance analysis  is reviewed with vendors on a regular basis. Contract terms are tracked  and audited. Automated notification when contract terms or hurdle rates  are exceed
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Centralized and standardized storage of contracts and extraction of terms from contracts for reporting purposes.  Exception analysis of commercial terms compliance and impacts identifying opportunities to improve future commercial terms and supply chain efficiencies.

bacr_question_full: Billing and Collections analysis to accelerate collections and reduce Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) and improve cash flow

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Billing and Collections processes are complex, subject to manual intervention, and disparate manual data collection, reconciliation, reporting and analysis.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Billing and Collections processes are partly automated, but still based on disparate data sourcing. Basic AR reporting (e.g. top 10%) is available.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Billing and Collection processes are automated, and based on data sourced from an integrated data repository. Billing terms and conditions are automatically applied. Detailed historic AR reporting is available, and basic AR scorecard has been developed.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Billing processes are automated using granular and timely data. Billing terms and conditions are automatically applied. Detailed information available in real-time to describe historic and current payment status . Future payment terms are set based on analysis of historic behaviour. Collection workflow based on simple rules.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Billing processes are automated using granular and timely data. Billing terms and conditions are automatically applied. Detailed information available in real-time to describe historic and current payment status. Future payment terms are set based on analysis of historic behaviour and/or 3rd party payment data. Automated collections decisioning, communications and actions based on predictive collections models & rules.

bacr_question_full: Procurement and Payment analysis to review purchase order compliance, manage goos receipts and manage suppliers to contract terms

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: No link between Purchase Orders and Invoices. Analyses are done based on aggregated data extracts for limited periods and prepared in Excel files. Analyses are manual and time consuming and only done periodically.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Country ERP solutions have integrated Purchasing and Accounts Payable modules – but it is only possible to analyse Suppliers performance at an aggregated level. Analysis is manually intensive.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Purchasing and AP data is linked in an ERP solution – but do not have the ability to work with data at the most granular data. Analyses are done on a regular basis, but still requires a lot of manual effort to prepare. Global view of Supplier performance and conditions are still limited as common definitions are not consistently used.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Purchasing and AP data is linked either in an ERP solution or data warehouse. Detailed analyses of Supplier performance and Supplier conditions are done on a regular basis – typically following the Closing, Budget & Planning and/or the season for renegotiations (with Suppliers)
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: The Group has an integrated data warehouse, where all purchasing data and accounts payable data are available and updated real-time or daily. Pre-defined and ad hoc analyses can be done whenever needed. Everything is based on common definitions.

bacr_question_full: Sub-ledger accounting analyis to create centralised accounting processes and practises that are easier and cheaper to maintain and change whilst remaining compliant with all regulations.  Reducing reconciliation time between ledgers.

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Financial Accounting Processes  are either manually created or hard-coded into individual operational systems. Summary-level accounting data only passed to GL. No detailed accounting data is passed to the Data Warehouse.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Financial Accounting processes are hard-coded into individual operational systems. Summary level data is passed to GL, but some account-level accounting data is available (e.g. interest accruals) to feed the Data Warehouse.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Financial Accounting processes are hard-coded into individual operational systems. Summary level data is passed to GL. The majority of account-level accounting data is available in the Data Warehouse and the reconciliation between the GL and Data Warehouse is significantly automated.  Manual Adjustments are only captured in the GL.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: An Accounting Hub solution is used for selected operational systems covering less complex requirements. Detailed accounting sub-ledger data is  generated and  integrated into the Data Warehouse for those operational systems, and the aggregated postings are passed to the GL.  Manual adjustments for these systems are originated in the sub-ledger and aggregated to the GL.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: The Accounting Hub covers all operational systems and lines of business. Detailed accounting sub-ledger data is  generated and  integrated into the Data Warehouse  for those operational systems. All manual adjustments are originated in the sub-ledger and workflow approved.  Aggregated postings are passed to the GL.

bacr_question_full: Fair Value and Hedge Accounting, to mitigate the impact of adverse movements in volatile assets and commodities (eg. Currency, interest rates, fuel etc.)

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Fair Value & Hedge Accounting processes are manually-intensive and utilise disparate sources of data which are subject to validation and integration effort.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Fair Value & Hedge Accounting is performed using a dedicated application which sources data directly from disparate sources.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Fair Value & Hedge Accounting is performed using a dedicated application, which sources data from a single integrated source.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Fair Value & Hedge Accounting is performed on a somewhat automated basis using a dedicated application, which sources  all of the required data from a single integrated source.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Fair Value and Hedge Accounting is delivered as part of an integrated Accounting Hub solution. Rules-based calculation and accounting functionality enables Fair Value and Hedge Accounting to be performed on a largely automated basis, including detailed audit trail.  Analytical toolset supports hedge optimisation analytics.

bacr_question_full: Asset Valuations, to comply with relevant accounting and tax standards for valuation and identify impairments on a timely basis

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Asset valuations are calculated on a aggregate basis using manually-intensive processes. Data is obtained from disparate sources and is subject to manual  validation and integration effort.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Asset valuations are calculated on a mix of aggregate and granular basis. Some integrated data is used, however much is still obtained from disparate sources. Manual effort to source, validate and integrate data is still significant.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Asset valuations are mostly calculated on a granular basis, and mostly use data from an integrated source. Manual effort to source, validate and integrate data is much reduced. Accounting calculations and rules are mostly hard-coded.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Asset valuations are based on statistical and analytical models and meets all relevant accounting standards. Data used is mostly available from an integrated source. The process, including identification of impairments and creation of accounting entries, is mostly automated, but often hard-coded. Any manual intervention is managed using workflow functionality.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Asset valuations are based on sophisticated statistical and analytical models and meets all relevant accounting standards. Granular, integrated and up-to-date data is available with minimal manual effort, and a rules-based Accounting Hub is used to perform calculations, apply Accounting rules, and create accounting entries. Any manual intervention is managed using workflow functionality.

bacr_question_full: Reserve Analytics, to accurately estimate and account for future losses and/or establish reserves in recognition of anticipated debts, impairments, warranties, loyalty program costs etc.

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Reserves are set based on average historic loss  or redemption rates. Data is manually sourced and integrated using desktop tools (e.g. Excel / Access).
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Introduction of basic statistical models to set reserves. Data is still obtained and integrated manually from multiple sources.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing:
Reserves are calculated using basic statistical models based on granular historic data.
Automation of processes leveraging integrated data.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating:
Reserves are calculated using more advanced statistical models based on granular historic data. 
Introduction of statistical techniques to more accurate calculate reserves balances using granular data
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Reserves use advanced statistically-derived and/or advanced analytical models based on granular historic and unstructured data, sourced from an integrated data repository. Models are executed on an automated basis, proven to be historically accurate, and resulting accounting and reporting is delivered on a timely basis.

bacr_question_full: Tax Management and Optimisation, to efficiently and automatically calculate tax values and produce appropriate tax reporting

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Tax Management is performed manually (e.g. Excel / Access) using feeds of data from disparate General Ledger / ERP and other operational systems. Substantial manual effort is required.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Tax Management is still performed using desktop-based applications (e.g. Excel, Access) however some automation of data sourcing from disparate General Ledger / ERP and other operational systems has been introduced.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Tax Management is performed using a dedicated solution which sources data directly from disparate General Ledger / ERP and other operational systems.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Tax management is undertaken using a largely automated dedicated solution, which sources the majority of the required data from a single integrated and validated source. Tax optimisation and planning is delivered using this same source of data.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: An Accounting Hub approach is used to deliver granular financial accounting, including tax calculations, and also tax aggregation and posting to the GL. Rules-based functionality enables tax rules to be maintained and updated easily. Tax return data can be produced on a largely automated basis with full drill-down and audit trail is available.

bacr_question_full: Reconciliation, Validation and Adjustment Analysis, to automate reconciliations, validations and adjustment processes as far as possible, and support audit trails of data to give confidence to accounting data users

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Reconciliation, Validation and Adjustment processes are fragmented and distributed widely across the organisation. They are largely manual, and involve extensive use of reports and spreadsheets.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Reconciliation and Validation are subject to some centralisation, with some use of common tools and processes.  However the underlying data upon which they operate is still fragmented, and needs to be sourced directly. Adjustments  are applied manually.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: A dedicated tool or solution is used to perform Reconciliation & Validation on a largely automated basis against data which is largely available from a single source. Adjustments are still primarily applied manually.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Reconciliation, Validation and Adjustments are centralised, with well-defined and documented responsibilities and processes. A dedicated tool or solution is used to perform these processes on a largely automated basis against data which is largely available from a single source.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Reconciliation, Validation and Adjustments are centralised and automated, with well-defined and documented responsibilities. A best-in-class tool or solution is used, with exceptions requiring action being delivered via workflow functionality. Adjustments are integrated into both financial systems and data warehouse/analytical systems.

bacr_question_full: Financial Consolidation, to provide timely, accurate and efficient reporting of consolidated financial information across multiple ERPs and legal entities

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Financial Consolidation is performed using desktop-based applications (e.g. Excel, Access), and relies on substantial manual effort to source, collate, map and integrate financial data. The financial close process is slow and top-line adjustments are only visible in the consolidated records.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Financial Consolidation is still performed using desktop-based applications (e.g. Excel, Access) however some automation of data sourcing from disparate General Ledger / ERP and other operational systems has been introduced. The financial close process is still time-consuming.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Financial Consolidation is delivered using a dedicated consolidation tool, however data is still sourced from disparate GL / ERP systems. Some improvements have been made to the speed of financial close.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Financial Consolidation is delivered using a dedicated consolidation tool which sources the required GL / ERP data from an integrated data repository. The financial close process has been accelerated, however the ability to drill-down is limited to the summary-level legal entity financial data.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: A best of breed Financial Consolidation solution is used, delivering an extremely fast financial consolidation process. Rules and mappings are maintained by financial analysts, requiring minimal IT development and maintenance. Financial information is fully integrated, and drill-down is available from summary to detail.

bacr_question_full: Functional Profit and Loss Statement, delivers functional PnLs for profit centers and segments including those not directly supported by the GL/ERP/Consolidation process

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Functional P&L  production is laborious and difficult. Reporting is almost exclusively done through Excel. Design and customisation of GL / ERP systems requires use of multiple segments resulting in a ‘thick’ GL, with high maintenance costs and poor performance. Minimal ability to drill from summary-level P&L to detailed data.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Functional P&Ls are manually produced using feeds from disparate General Ledger / ERP. Substantial manual effort is required. BI tools are deployed but with limited capability to provide drill downs from summary-level P&L to detailed data.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Functional P&Ls are automated and produced  using a BI tool which sources data directly from disparate General Ledger / ERP and other operational systems. Manual processes have been substantially reduced. Ability to drill from summary-level P&L to detail is limited by granularity of data sourcing.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Both the ERP / GL, sub-ledgers and operational systems are fed into an integrated warehouse with the links between the GL and Sub GL and other Operating Systems established. These transactions are reported out of the warehouse using a BI tool.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: An Accounting Hub is  used to deliver the granular financial reporting capability. Functional and segment-level P&Ls are delivered easily by the use of segments which are resident in the sub ledgers. The reporting segments are now maintained in the sub-ledgers with the appropriate drill-down capabilities.

bacr_question_full: Revenue Analytics to provide knowledge to the enterprise of the components of the mix of the revenue being generated and the margins associated with these products

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Actual sales, forecast and plans are rolled up at an aggregated level , usually using a manual process to acquire data.  Typically done in Excel or Access .
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Revenue analytics is performed at a hierarchy level but based on summary-level data. Some manual intervention is required for data acquisition.  Mainly used to understand components of revenue, including product sales and ancillary revenues
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Revenue Analytics is performed on a more granular basis, which enables deeper insights to the components of revenue.  Results can feed downstream applications at an aggregated level.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Detailed revenue data is automatically sourced from transactional and / or ERP system.  Analysis can be performed understand the underlying components and feed downstream applications.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Revenue Analytics is used extensively across the organisation. It uses best-in-class analytical techniques and a broad range of high quality, integrated data.   Sophisticated model exists which calculates revenue components.  Data is at a granular level which enables a multi-dimensional view of revenue.

bacr_question_full: GL, AP, and HR Expense Analytics and Optimisation, providing assistance in managing costs associated with HR, suppliers and other expenses

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: GL, AP, HR and Expense data is done is silos, with minimal  standardisation. Focus is primarily on the GL, AP, HR and Expense processes themselves.  One off reporting takes place but is not shared across the organisation.  Conflicting reporting and calculation definitions are possible due to lack of integration.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: GL, AP, HR and Expense data is widely distributed across the organisation, with little standarisation and integration. maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: GL, AP, HR and Expense data is sourced and integrated on at least a monthly basis, primarily at a summary-level, however it is not integrated with other non-finance data domains. Some centralised reporting and analysis is performed, largely focused on aggregated results
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: The majority of GL, AP, HR and Expense data is integrated in a single, integrated data warehouse or mart. Analysis across multiple dimensions, and drill-down to detailed transactions is available
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: GL, AP, HR and Expense processes are efficient and automated. Detailed data from across the organisation is updated and integrated daily, as well as with other non-finance data and multi-structured data. Sophisticated analytics on this domains  is used as a strategic planning and negotiating tool, is used to identify and manage policy exceptions, and is used to inform employee performance appraisals.
