bacr_question_full: Activity-Based Costing, assisting with developing more sophisticated and granular ABC models to support more accurate profitability analytics and better understanding of  cost drivers

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: ABC process is a high-level Excel based model and may have multiple versions by business unit or analysis objective.  Difficult to maintain and update, and possibly inconsistent across the organization.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: ABC process is performed on an infrequent basis (annual or less). It is a manual process which relies on manual data collection / entry, and uses spreadsheets to perform calculations. Calculated unit-costs are done at a higher level of granularity (Category / Product Type vs. Class / SKU)
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: ABC process is still performed annually and may use spreadsheets or an ABC/cost-modelling tool, however most of the required data is available from a single, integrated source.  Calculated unit-costs include breakdown by channel, however many costs are done at an average level.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: ABC process is performed more frequently (e.g. quarterly/monthly) using an ABC/cost-modelling tool. Multiple cost models are produced (e.g. standard/budgeted unit costs vs. actual unit costs).  Could be used to feed downstream analytics or applications.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: ABC process is automated, and is integrated with the wider profitability modelling processes within the organisation (e.g. customer profitability, lifetime value). It uses a single, integrated source of input data, which includes detailed process metrics. It is updated frequently, and Is able to  be modified quickly with “what if”  capability and multiple iterations

bacr_question_full: Future / Lifetime Value, analytics that calculate net present values for products, categories, segments, and customer or prospects

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Excel based model not fed from any upstream application.  Usually a stand-alone or one-off model.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: BI / Excel-based NPV models for key products/segments using summarised results from current/historic profit model
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Basic customer-level NPV model for existing product holdings only, using projected results from current/historic profit model.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Propensity models for some key products used to enhance customer-level model with attrition models for existing product holdings, and propensity to buy models for new products.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Full Future/Lifetime Value model for individual customers which includes comprehensive coverage of: Projected cashflows from existing product holdings; Attrition models for existing product holdings, and for Customer attrition; Propensity to buy and Life Stage progression models for new products.; Behavioural usage models for non-contractual products

bacr_question_full: Profitability Analytics and Optimisation which maximises the business value achieved through the use of Profitability and Future Value models

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Non-integrated profitability model results which manually feed analytical models.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Profitability results are used to deliver summary-level and individual customer reports to managers.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Profitability results are also used to support product development, product pricing, segment-based offers,
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Profitability results are also used operationally to deliver information and guidance to staff on customer retention, customer experience, pricing and other operational decisions (e.g. fee refunds)
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Automated process with ability to measure, monitor and track profitability improvement opportunities.  Used extensively across the organisation to support a wide range of strategic, tactical and operational decision-making.

bacr_question_full: Performance Management and KPIs to improve consistency and quality in how performance is measured and managed and reducing costs of production of these metrics

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Simple KPI reporting functions are produced for use at an executive level for senior management.  Manual data acquisition from non-integrated sources results in reduced response time.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Performance management is performed independently by many separate functions within the organisation using disparate data, which need to be manually sourced and/or integrated.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Responsibility for some performance management and KPI production is centralised however data is still fragmented and is subject to manual sourcing, integration and data quality activities.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Performance management and KPI production is centralised, and most data is available from a single, integrated source. KPIs and other measures are clearly defined and agreed, cover key business functions, and are aligned with strategic objectives. Drill-down from summary-level to detail is available (e.g. total business->business unit->individual manager)
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Performance management is part of the culture of the organisation and is executed on a centralised and co-ordinated basis using an integrated set of validated and quality-assured data.  A comprehensive range of KPIs and other measures are clearly defined and agreed, and cover both strategic and operational performance, using best-in-class data and reporting/BI/Dashboard tools are used to calculate and deliver information to end-users.

bacr_question_full: Inventory Analytics, to determine the investment that results in the minimisation of out of stocks balanced against optimal stock levels

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Periodic Excel spreadsheet of inventory done at an aggregated level and manually sourced.  Single point in time solution. Manual, infrequent silo’d, summarised, reporting of inventory in each location. Typically  delivered via spreadsheet based on point in time information.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Simple reporting of inventory performance based on aggregated results using BI tools and data acquired form sub-level systems. Integrated view of inventory across all locations in the supply chain, Still point in time, using current data but BI tool based allowing slice and dice analysis
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Reporting and analysis based data collected form multiple sources – some of which may be done manually.  Non-granular approach, primarily performed at a category or aggregated level.  Optimization capability done at a local level, highly focused on managing across the entire supply chain. Integrated view of inventory across all locations in the supply chain, Still point in time, using current data but BI tool based allowing slice and dice analysis
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Sophisticated reporting and forecasting of inventory based on historical trend analysis which can be shared across the organization and leverages integrated data sources.  Introduction of higher level predictive modeling techniques to predict trends. Ability to model changes to supply chain constraints  (cycle times, lead times, MOQs etc) to identify opportunities to optimise future inventory levels to meet forecast demand and sustain/increase availability by tuning ordering constraints
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Automated , integrated inventory analytics solution using  sophisticated modeling tools which enable analysis of stocking levels,  overstock, waste / slippage and optimal inventory projections based on predictive analytics using historical data and emerging trend analysis.  Results are used to optimize or improve cash flow. Automated modelling and tuning of optimal supply chain constraints and inventory levels to meet future demand at the most economical costs making most effective use of current supply chain resources

bacr_question_full: Financial Budgetting, Planning and Forecasting to simplify and automate the budgeting, planning and forecasting process through the usage of high quality consistent data to drive improvements in speed, efficiency and costs.

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Static budget done annually, usually using spread sheets and not shared across the organization.  Lack of detail minimises the usefulness.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Budgeting, Planning and Forecasting is performed independently by many separate functions within the organisation using disparate data, which needs to be manually  sourced and/or integrated. Slow budget process cycle time. Low levels of accuracy (actuals : budget)
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Responsibility for Budgeting, Planning and Forecasting is centralised however data is still fragmented and is subject to manual sourcing, integration and data quality activities. Moderate levels of accuracy (actuals : budget)
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Budgeting, Planning and Forecasting is mostly centralised, and the majority of required data is available from a single, integrated source. A specialised Budgeting, Planning & Forecasting tool is used. High levels of accuracy (actuals : budget)
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Budgeting, Planning and Forecasting is a largely automated process, utilising data from a single, validated and quality-assured source. Best-in-class tool provides Budgeting, Planning and Forecasting functionality with minimal manual intervention. Fast budget process cycle time. Very high levels of accuracy (actuals : budget)

bacr_question_short: Business Process Analytics and Optimisation to analyse
bacr_question_full: Business Process Analytics and Optimisation to analyse, understand and optimizse business processes in order to improve efficiency, reduce costs and increase customer satisfaction

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Traditional ‘time & motion’ studies, which can be resource-intensive, costly, and disruptive to the business.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Business process analytics and optimisation is largely manual and based on traditional observation, analysis, time & motion studies and summary-level data.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Business process analytics and optimisation uses detailed data to support analysis and optimisation, however this needs to be manually sourced and integrated. Analytical processes are a mixture of manual investigation / insight and use of analytical tools and techniques.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Business process analytics and optimisation uses a range of structured and multi-structured data, and advanced analytical techniques. A structured process exists to deploy process improvements into production. A track record of process optimisation driving improvements in revenue, cost or customer experience can be demonstrated.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Business process analytics and optimisation is used extensively across the organisation. A broad range of processes are regularly monitored to identify deterioration or specific areas to focus on. A broad range of structured and multi-structured data is used, which is available with minimal manual sourcing and integration effort, and a broad range of advanced analytical techniques. A structured process exists to deploy improvements into production, and to track improvements and monitor over time.

bacr_question_short: Cashflow Generation analytics to generate detailed
bacr_question_full: Cashflow Generation analytics to generate detailed, accurate and granular cash flow data to support a range of treasury, reporting, liquidity and other functions

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Cashflow modelling occurs only at a summary-level. Input data requires manual sourcing, integration and validation.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Cashflow modelling is shifting from on a summary-level towards (more) granular cashflows generated for some portfolios / products. Cashflow generation is executed using hard-coded routines which require significant technical/IT effort to maintain. Data is sourced from disparate operational systems and other sources
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Cashflow modelling and generation takes place for portfolios / products using a single, integrated and validated set of input data. Significant coverage of granular cashflow generation.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Cashflow analytics and modelling are based on an integrated and validated set of input data. Models are developed using rules-based functionality and generally generate cashflows on a granular basis (agreement/contract-level).
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Cashflow analytics and modelling uses best-in-class tools against a single, integrated and validated set of input data. Models are developed using rules-based functionality and generally generate cashflows on a granular basis (agreement/contract-level).

bacr_question_full: Capital Planning and Management, to plan for capital requirements, allocate capital within the organisation and set cost of capital

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Capital Planning & Management is only performed based on summary-level data.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Capital Planning & Management is performed largely using summary-level data which is sourced into application- or function-specific data mart(s). Deeper levels of granular analysis requires integration of source data for each new use case.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Capital Planning & Management is generally supported through dedicated Treasury- or line-of-business data warehousing. Integration and aggregation of Capital Planning & Management data for analytical purposes is still dependent on application centric data architecture.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Capital Planning & Management analysis and reporting is generally delivered as integrated part of enterprise data & analytical capability, although some aspects may still rely on Treasury- or line-of-business data warehousing, or application-specific data architecture components. All data loaded at least daily.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Capital Planning & Management analysis and reporting is delivered as integrated part of enterprise data & analytical capability, using common validated and quality-assured data with audit trail. All data loaded at least daily, and where relevant / required on near real-time basis. Regular analysis & reporting performed using shared tools and services, and well within speed-of-business and/or regulatory demands.

bacr_question_full: Liquidity Management analytics manage short and long-term positions, including intra-day liquidity and risk, to meet payment and settlement obligations on a timely basis, under both normal and stressed conditions

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Liquidity management policies and standards are not yet sufficient to comply with regulatory standards. They may be under development. Adequate tools to support intraday liquidity management are not yet in place.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Liquidity management policies and standards meet minimum regulatory standards for intra-day liquidity management. Reporting at summary Market/Liquidity Risk and Funding/Liquidity Risk levels. Deeper levels of granular analysis requires integration of source data for each new use case. Functional data marts are common.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Liquidity analytics and reporting supported through line-of-business data warehousing. Integration and aggregation of liquidity data still dependent on app centric data architecture for granular analytics.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Single source of liquidity management data based on a common integrated enterprise data platform supporting aggregation and analysis across the interplay of liquidity with assets liabilities and capital. Comprehensive analytical capabilities available. Materially compliant with BCBS 239 but some legacy / manual processing still evident (e.g. stress scenarios).
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Fully integrated risk and collateral management and reporting environment. Liquidity management policy and practice supported by a data and analytic centric information architecture. Ad-hoc analytics requiring granular level data across multiple dimensions (asset, tenor, time period etc.) can be fulfilled well within speed-of-business demands. Data capabilities support streaming and real-time market data updates.

bacr_question_full: Risk Scenario and Stress Test - vital parts of best practice risk management

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Limited or no formal  Scenario and Stress testing is in place.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Formal and regular Scenario/Stress testing is in place, but on an infrequent basis (e.g. annual). Scenario/Stress testing involves  manually creating stressed inputs , executing models and comparing the results.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Formal and regular Scenario/Stress testing  is in place on a more frequent basis.  The production of stressed  input data sets is well documented, based on defined rules and is partially automated (e.g. use of templates/scripts). The measurement and comparison of scenario  results  is repeatable (e.g. use of standard reports)
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Formal and regular Scenario/Stress testing largely automated. The production of stressed  input data sets is  well documented, and largely automated (e.g. using rule engine).  Some use of advanced  scenario/stress testing methods such as Monte Carlo and other Stochastic techniques. Automated
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Scenario/Stress testing is fully automated and integrated with the Risk and Capital Model development, decisioning and deployment processes. The production of stressed  input data sets is  fully rules-based and automated. Widespread use of advanced  scenario/stress testing methods such as Monte Carlo and other Stochastic techniques. Execution of scenario/stress test models , review of output, and is also automated as part of an overall workflow.

bacr_question_full: Asset and Liability Management analytics will assist in effective management of interest rate and liquidity risks

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Asset& Liability Management is not institutionalized . It is managed by the CFO and/or Controller as an ad-hoc process, largely using summary-level data  which is manually sourced.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Asset & Liability Management  is performed largely using summary-level data which is sourced into application- or function-specific data mart(s). Deeper levels of granular analysis requires integration of source data for each new use case.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Asset & Liability Management is generally supported through dedicated Treasury- or line-of-business data warehousing. Integration and aggregation of ALM data for analytical purposes is still dependent on application centric data architecture.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: ALM analysis and reporting is generally delivered as integrated part of enterprise data & analytical capability, although some aspects may still rely on Treasury or line-of-business data warehousing, or application-specific data architecture components. All data loaded at least daily, and where relevant / required on near real-time basis
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: ALM analysis and reporting is delivered as integrated part of enterprise data & analytical capability, using common validated and quality-assured data with audit trail. All data loaded at least daily, and where relevant / required on near real-time basis. Analysis & reporting performed in-database using shared tools and services, and well within speed-of-business and/or regulatory demands or if dedicated ALM tools/applications are used then they are best-in-class and use the enterprise data.

bacr_question_full: Funds Transfer Pricing analytics will enable central management of net interest margin and cost of funds, along with fair and reasonable pricing of Cost/value of funds attributable to each customer contract

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Funds Transfer Pricing is not calculated or is performed on GL balances as part of the monthly close process by applying simple pool rates in excel.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Funds Transfer Pricing occurs only at a summary (portfolio) level on a monthly basis, using a desktop tool (e.g. excel).  Input data requires manual sourcing, integration and validation.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Funds Transfer Pricing generally occurs monthly, at a summary(portfolio) level and uses an application-centric approach, with limited sophistication (simple pool rates and other non DCF methodologies). Data is sourced from disparate operational systems and other sources on a largely automated basis into an application data mart. Limited drill-down to granular levels is availability
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Funds Transfer Pricing uses best-in-class, business user configurable tools to inform funding, pricing, liquidity and planning decisions on a monthly basis. A single validated set of granular input data is sourced from an integrated, cross-functional data warehouse.  A comprehensive set of FTP methodologies are supported, which are  matched to the funding characteristics of each instrument.  FTP is mainly calculated at the individual instrument level with some portfolio level pooling, as part of a comprehensive profitability model to support consistent multi-dimensional analysis.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Funds Transfer Pricing uses best-in-class, business user configurable tools to inform funding, pricing, liquidity and planning decisions on a daily (or intra-day) basis. A single validated set of granular input data is sourced from an integrated, cross-functional data warehouse.  A comprehensive set of FTP methodologies are supported, which are  matched to the funding characteristics of each instrument.  FTP is calculated at the individual instrument level as part of a comprehensive profitability model to support consistent multi-dimensional analysis.

bacr_question_short: FX and Trading Book Management analytics will identify
bacr_question_full: FX and Trading Book Management analytics will identify, measure and managed the risk of losses arising from adverse movements in market prices (E..g equity or commodity prices, interest or FX rates)

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Based on aggregated data in spreadsheet models. Barely meets minimum regulatory requirements.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Point solutions and heavy dependence on spreadsheet models. Data marts proliferate, minimal referential integrity and data governance necessary to meet minimum regulatory requirements. Non-scalable architecture, incremental changes increasingly costly.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Fit for purpose applications and some degree of integration to support regulatory reporting but data-marts still proliferate within FX sensitive lines of business. Vision & strategy orienting towards analytic and data centric architecture & some progress on roadmap.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: FXR integrated into ‘up-stream’ enterprise risk framework. Integrated transaction and position data with streaming FX and IR data supporting near real-time VaR. Data and analytic centric vision and strategy with a well defined roadmap.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Simultaneous FXR and IRR hedging strategies capability within an integrated enterprise risk management platform. Business agility enabled through analytic ecosystem architecture. Integrated transaction and position data with streaming FX and IR data supporting near real-time VaR

bacr_question_short: Interest (Risk) Rate Management analytics will identify
bacr_question_full: Interest (Risk) Rate Management analytics will identify, measure and manage the interest rate risk (in the banking book) in order to limit losses from unexpected interest rate changes

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Based on aggregated data in spreadsheet models to meet at least minimum regulatory requirements.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Point solutions and heavy dependence on spreadsheet models. Data marts proliferate, minimal referential integrity and data governance necessary to meet minimum regulatory requirements. Non-scalable architecture, incremental changes increasingly costly.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Fit for purpose applications and some degree of integration to support regulatory reporting but data-marts still proliferate within IR sensitive lines of business. Vision & strategy orienting towards analytic and data centric architecture & some progress on roadmap.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: IRR integrated into ‘up-stream’ enterprise risk framework. Integrated transaction and position data with streaming FX and IR data supporting near real-time VaR. Data and analytic centric vision and strategy with a well defined roadmap.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Simultaneous IRR and FXR hedging strategies capability within an integrated enterprise risk management platform. Business agility enabled through analytic ecosystem architecture. . Integrated transaction and position data with streaming FX and IR data supporting near real-time VaR.

bacr_question_short: Statutory Financial Reporting analytics enable accurate
bacr_question_full: Statutory Financial Reporting analytics enable accurate, timely, and effcicient production of financial statements and other statutory reports with minimal data collection, validation, reconciliation and adjustments

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Statutory Financial Reports are manually prepared from multiple, disparate data sources. Considerable time is spent collecting, validating and integrating data prior to its use in reporting. Multiple reporting, BI, spreadsheet tools are used.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Data for core summary-level financial reporting is available from multiple sources. Most other / more detailed data needs to be collected from multiple sources using multiple tools and is subject to manual processes before use.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Data for core summary-level financial reporting is available from single source (based however on multiple data sources) using multiple tools and is subject to manual processes before use.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Most of the required data is available from a single, integrated source, although a small number of other data sources may exist. Regular reports & extracts are available on a largely automated basis , as well as ad-hoc reports and queries using a single reporting/BI tool.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading:
Statutory reports are produced on a largely automated basis from a single, integrated source of validated data. 
Some companies may have outsourced this process, delivering data to eg. Audit Companies.

bacr_question_full: Sales Reporting covers the timely, accurate and efficient reporting of sales achievement and performance across the entire organisation, identifying sales performance and discounting and other sales KPIs

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Sales reporting is aggregated summary data and there is no link to detailed products and sales orders. Everything is managed in elementary tooling, e.g. Excel. Reporting takes place on an infrequent basis.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Sales reporting for different products is delivered on a fragmented basis across different sources/siloes of data, and requires significant manual effort. Reporting takes place on an infrequent (monthly) basis.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Sales reporting is centralised, however the data which is required is obtained from many different sources and requires integration and validation effort. Reporting is on a more frequent basis (minimum weekly)
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Sales reporting is generally centralised and utilises a common source of integrated data and reporting tools. Reporting is possible on a daily basis, and ability to drill down to granular level to identify areas and causes of poor performance.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Sales reporting exists as part of an integrated environment which enables close monitoring and reporting of performance against objectives, targets and plans.  It utilises a common source of high quality, validated and integrated data subject to comprehensive data governance. Daily and intra-day monitoring and alerts are supported. Advanced analytics are used to more accurately pinpoint causes of poor performance.

bacr_question_short: Regulatory and Compliance Reporting is aimed at the accurate
bacr_question_full: Regulatory and Compliance Reporting is aimed at the accurate, timely and efficient delivery of regulatory and compliance reports and data, consistent with statutory financial reporting

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Each different Regulatory and Compliance reporting requirement is gathered manually from multiple sources using elementary tools e.g. spreadsheets.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Each different Regulatory and Compliance reporting requirement is delivered on a siloed basis, using different data sourcing and tools with some level of automation.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Data for core summary-level financial reporting is available from a single source, however most other / more detailed data needs to be collected from multiple sources using multiple tools, and is subject to manual processes before use.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Most of the required data is available from a single, integrated source, although some supplementary data sources may exist. Regular reports & extracts to downstream regulatory and compliance solutions are available on a largely automated basis. Ad-hoc reports and queries can easily be produced using a single reporting/BI tool.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Regulatory and Compliance reporting requirements are addressed on an systematic and integrated basis. A comprehensive common data platform is used. Where possible common calculation and reporting tools are used, however specific solutions for particular pieces of regulation/compliance may be used if appropriate. Data used is clearly documented and understood, subject to comprehensive data governance, and data quality and lineage can be clearly demonstrated.

bacr_question_full: Performance Reporting covers the timely, accurate and efficient reporting of performance across a wide range of metrics for the entire organisation

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Performance reporting takes place on demand only, based on aggregated summary data. Manual rekeying data into elementary tooling, e.g. Excel.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Performance reporting is delivered on a fragmented basis across different sources/siloes of data, and requires significant manual effort. Reporting takes place on an infrequent (monthly) basis.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Performance reporting is centralised, however the data which is required is obtained from many different sources and requires integration and validation effort. Reporting is on a more frequent basis (minimum weekly)
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Performance reporting is generally centralised and utilises a common source of integrated data and reporting tools. Reporting is possible on a daily basis, and ability to drill down to granular level to identify areas and causes of poor performance.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Performance reporting exists as part of an integrated environment which enables close monitoring and reporting of performance against objectives, targets and plans.  It utilises a common source of high quality, validated and integrated data subject to comprehensive data governance. Daily and intra-day monitoring and alerts are supported. Advanced analytics are used to more accurately pinpoint causes of poor performance.

bacr_question_full: Exception Reporting is the timely, accurate and efficient reporting of unexpected variances and other exceptions for the whole organisation

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Exception reporting is based on aggregated summary level data, requires huge manual effort in gathering and preparing the report and it is (often) static.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Exception reporting is fragmented and distributed widely across the organisation. Exception rules, variances and parameters are not routinely quantified. It is largely manual, and involves extensive manual review of reports and spreadsheets.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Exception reporting  is subject to some centralisation, with some use of common tools and processes. Some exception rules, variances and parameters are quantified and agreed. However the underlying data upon which is operates is still fragmented, and needs to be sourced directly.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Exception reporting is centralised, with well-defined and documented responsibilities and processes. Exception rules, variances and parameters are routinely quantified and agreed. A dedicated tool or solution is used to perform these processes on a largely automated basis against data which is largely available from a single source.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Exception reporting is centralised, with well-defined and documented responsibilities and processes. Exception rules, variances and parameters are routinely quantified and agreed. A best-in-class tool or solution is used to perform comparisons and process exception rules on an automated basis. All data is available from a single, integrated and validated source. Exceptions requiring action are delivered via workflow functionality.

bacr_question_short: Executive Dashboards provide direct access for executives an
bacr_question_full: Executive Dashboards provide direct access for executives and other key decision-makers to comprehensive and up to date consolidated information to support and enhance management decisions

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Executive reporting is not common in an organization. Reporting only exists on ad-hoc basis and requires huge manual interventions to collect data and aggregate. No standards exist for reports.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Executive reporting is largely paper based and consists largely of standard reports, delivered on an infrequent basis (monthly or less) from disparate sources of data. Requests for non-standard information by executives are delivered via largely manual processes.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Paper reports are supplemented by direct executive access to electronic reporting via a standard BI/Reporting tool. The available reports are prepared automatically but utilise data which is sourced from a number of disparate sources and is subject to specific quality and validation processes.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Executives have direct access to Dashboards which deliver information sourced primarily from a single integrated set of validated and agreed data, which is updated on a daily basis. Non-standard reports can be quickly delivered by staff from the same integrated source.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Executives have direct access to comprehensive Dashboards based on a single integrated set of validated and agreed data which is updated on a daily or intra-day basis. Dashboards display information using a variety of appropriate visualisations (e.g. charts, geographic, RAG status), with slice/drill-down capabilities. Exceptions and potential issues are highlighted based on defined business rules.

bacr_question_short: Functional Unit Management is the ability
bacr_question_full: Functional Unit Management is the ability to monitor and act effectively to monitor business processes so as to  resolve business process bottlenecks and make proper resource planning

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Basic / Limited level of business process monitoring with manual data collection, reporting. Depend on IT or other business units to get these reports, using best practices to allocate correct number of staff to the field.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Automated reporting of what is happening on operations activity regarding business unit performance & business service level performance.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Using historic data of granular performance metrics, staff Hr data and applying analytical techniquest to uncerstand clusters and affinity analysis who is performing well and what are the indicators. Taking action to make others more efficent based on these insights.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Applying advaned analytical techniques to all application , HR and  performance data  to predict performance indicators, decide on which teams capacity to increase, taking into consideration seasonality or competitive product/service effect.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Using real time streaming data to detect anomaly transaction density – which can be caused by unpredicted system error, or regulation effect which is adhoc - , create some alert events to be able to act rapidly preventing any kind of service outage or quality problem.  Classifiying business services based on skillset requirements and moving correct amount of optimum skilled staff on time with minimum labor cost. Optimizing overtime and shift costs using deep dive analtyics.

bacr_question_short: Service Cost Management is calculating the profitability of
bacr_question_full: Service Cost Management is calculating the profitability of customers based on actual business activiites and operating costs necessary to service a customer or account

maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Ability to analyze cost to serve in broad terms by manually merging and analysing customer demographics and product purchases and costs associated with final delivery

bacr_question_short: Predictive Maintenance Optimization is a proactive approach
bacr_question_full: Predictive Maintenance Optimization is a proactive approach to operations and maintenance, improving asset performance, customer experience and CAPEX/OPEX optimisation through proactive maintenance planning and current and projected condition of the individual assets to eliminate non-value added efforts and understand failure modes and effects analysis

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Maintenance analysis based on aggregated Asset logs and basic service usage trends. Small portfolio of events (<20) detected using static traditional data sources. e.g. vehicle performance measures (stop/start, RPM, MPG, thrust, etc…) Events detected on weekly / monthly basis with dependency on load of core data feeds.  May be manual feeds from equipment upon periodic inspection and download of data
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Expand maintenance analysis based on asset traces with initial isolation of main path to failures, affinity failure for root cause identification. Expanding portfolio of events (20- 50) covering a limited range of business objectives /  data sources incl. history and using more sophisticated transactional event detection routines. Data latency constraints being addressed to improve performance of events – daily / weekly. Identify patterns of equipment performance at a unit and even the beginnings of fleet patterns.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Enhance maintenance activities with sophisticated trend analysis using a large variety of data sources (device logs, workforce tickets and reports, …). Medium portfolio of events (50-200) covering a wider range of business objectives /  data sources incl. history and using more sophisticated transactional event detection routines. Data latency constraints have been addressed and most are now executed on a daily basis.  Using more data to develop predictive patterns.  Beyond what happened, not starting to find why failures are occurring that can lead to new predictive maintenance schedules.  Confidence in the accuracy of maintenance prediction now drives all scheduled maintenance activity across the entire fleet
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Apply advanced analytic techniques in maintenance analysis to predict service critical impacting failures and to help to identify proactive and preventive field actions maximizing profitability, availability and scalability of the field operations activities. Medium to large portfolio (200-500) of events, mostly detected on daily basis from an expanding range of data sources including transactions and interactions. (Including online). Some intra-day event detection performed, particularly for digital channels. Established set of event detection methodologies are utilised depending on timeliness and complexity of data.  Finding patterns in relational failures cause by other parts interactions.  Developing detailed maintenance plans based on CBM principles using the patterns of failure that lead to unscheduled down time.   Performing maintenance on items that are not yet due because of relationships with parts in the current maintenance schedule
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Proactive and methodical approach to mainteance optimization by applying model development, learning and prediction of asset failures, propensity to fail. Utilise multiple data sources including real-time asset condition monitoring  to detect and predict abnormal infrastructure and operational behavorials leading to increase costs and impact Customer Experience. Large portfolio of events (500+) detected on a real-time / intraday / daily basis from a rich variety of data sources including transactions, interactions and external data. Ak8dvanced event detection routines such as machine learning finds unusual patterns of behaviour and detects changes in behaviour over time. Events are combined to specialise customer treatment and increase response. Active test and  learn methodology continuously trials new event types.  Actually diagnosing the failure to help prep for the maintenance event, leads to better tech resourcing, better inventory planning, faster maintenance time, improved customer service, maximum utilization of equipment, maximum productivity of equipment.

bacr_question_short: Warranty Management is the reduction of product warranty cos
bacr_question_full: Warranty Management is the reduction of product warranty costs related to recalls, repair, return and analysis of root cause from the warranty claim to improve product quality from the manufacturing location

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Gather warranty claims data and begin to analyze for patterns of behavior by part, dealer product, region and manufacturing plant
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Using the warranty claim patterns, begin to identify warranty claim fraud and spikes in claims by part, dealer, regions etc.  Start to identify the rules that lead to automatic process of the claim as it fits normal claim patterns and hold out for manual review those claims that do not fit the patterns of acceptable claims.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Using statistical control analytics to trace claim back to root cause…  was it a supplier, a MFG practice, improper maintenance, etc.  By building on the work already done, the customer should now be able to automatically pay at least 90% of claims, identify the root cause of those claims and work with the offending cause organizations to put corrective actions in place.  The customer should be able to identify the breadth of the warranty exposure, identify all products in the field that share the same failure characteristic and begin to scope the exposure to the organization in a matter of hours rather than days, weeks or months
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Potentially bringing in sensor data from the product in the field could help identify a pattern of failure inside warranty periods that could lead to preventative steps by customer and field service to proactively repair the product in the field at significantly less cost to the organization.  This significantly shortens the exposure time in the field and helps the offending organization react to the problem much faster therefore limiting the amount of tainted product that leaves the manufacturing/supplier site.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Full integration of data though out the product lifecycle that leads to immediate identification of failure patterns through warranty and maintenance data combined with the manufacturing/supplier data , the customer and dealer data to be able to perform complete track and trace analytics through lot and serial number tracking, regardless of the industry, enabling an immediate (minutes/hours) identification of the root cause and notification of all affected parties, implementing a recovery plan for each product in the plant, at the supplier, in finished goods, in the distribution channel and at the customers site.

bacr_question_full: Sales / Value-based Compensation aims to use analytics to monitor the appropriate application of sales and incentive compensation

bacr_question_full: Document Fraud analytics aims to monitor documents provided by customers, suppliers and employees to detect fraudulent anomalies quickly and avoid losses

Big data infrastructure that provides access to and integrates all required data sources across the organization.
