Audit preparation is mostly electronic, accreditation common. DUR is automated and alerts are case-specific; alert fatigue is minimal.  Acute-care, chronic care transitions are regular and consistent. JIT logistics have 2% write-offs due to diversion/ OOS/overstock/unsaleables. clinical time is a significant factor, with PQA standards utilized.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Care teams are well coordinated, with EHR communications interoperable with analytics to assist practitioners with clinical results.  Computerized clinical decision-making is incorporated into practices and driven by Evidence-based medicine. Cost–effectiveness studies consistently achieve top results.  Audit preparation is streamlined, accreditation consistently maximized. JIT logistics regularly achieve below 2% write-offs due to diversion/OOS/overstock/unsaleables

bacr_question_full: Contract Compliance Management - ensuring efficient contract compliance management supporting rapid change management actions for non-compliant vendors

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: No automated approach, manual collection of data with limited historical data available, non timely decision for non compliant vendors  - lack of root cause analysis  - no insight for better negotiations.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Basic KPIs defined, Semi-automated approach and data collection, no full visibility on vendor compliance, delay in action implementation – delayed supplier change  management -  basic  root cause analysis . No linkage between KPIs and contract terms
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Timely and on demand  vendor compliance analysis  based on historical data using a manual process – centralized storage of contracts in standardized format -   manual root case analysis with corrective action plans  managed manually
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: All supplier compliance related metrics and KPis  defined and implemented - Automated dashboards that drive supplier contract compliance ensure visibility on relevant KPI’s- automated and timely reporting of non-compliant suppliers  -  automated  root case analysis with clear corrective action plan . Full impact analysis of non-compliance on service, revenue and margin
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Timely decision making on cost optimization decisions – Predictive non compliance analysis - rapid change management for suppliers out of compliance ensuring cost optimization – optimized contract negotiations considering impacts on risk, revenue and margin

bacr_question_full: Suppplier Collaboration - Build a close working relationship to jointly improve service, availability and efficiency whilst reducing costs and inventory

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging:
Manual sharing of demand data, typically sales history at chain level, by week/month either via a basic sales portal or file sharing (Excel)
Supplier performance measured using spreadsheets
No understanding of the impact of poor supplier performance on downstream supply chain service
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Development of a sales portal to share demand data with suppliers. No active collaboration between parties
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing:
Automated Sharing of sales forecast data at location level by day
Supplier performance dashboards  developed in BI tool
Portals used to manage purchase order status tracking to identify potential supply issues
Impact analysis of joint supply chain failures on service and inventory
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Calculation and sharing of future purchase order forecasts, future promotion plans to support joint planning and new launch activities In order to improve overall supply chain service and optimise inventory levels  driving lower costs and reduce lead-times. Active collaboration between partners
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Active sharing of limited basket sales data and inventory data  by location to support improved operational KPIs, causal analysis and impact analysis of supply chain failures. Close collaboration between partners to address joint challenges and improve costs, efficiencies and service.

bacr_question_full: Supplier Performance Management - Analytics ensuring efficient governance of vendor and category performance, profitability, and compliance while meeting customer expectations

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: No automated approach, manual collection of data with limited historical data available, aggregated information analysed,  product centric approach rather than vendor, limited insights that are not available in non timely decision, no control over number and quality of suppliers
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Basic KPIs defined, Semi-automated approach and data collection, limited to major categories only, no full visibility on vendor performance and compliance, delay in action implementation, no thresholds defined, unclear approval process
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Timely and on demand  vendor performance analysis with a granularity on the category level in an automated exception driven process – based on historical data using a manual approval process – centralized storage of contracts in standardized format
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: all cross-functional  supplier management related metrics and KPis  defined and implemented - Vendor scorecard implemented  Balancing supply & demand measurements - vigorous insight driven vetting and approval process – proper trading and compliance partner management, cost efficient vendor management
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Predictive Vendor and industry level analysis , identifying potential supply failures or supply opportunities with  proactive decisions  on cost optimization, service improvement and efficiency – Cost Efficient category management - clear buying thresholds  for all categories based on historical contracts and vendor analysis - Automated processes across hundreds of vendors/categories

bacr_question_short: Spend Analytics - improve margins through product
bacr_question_full: Spend Analytics - improve margins through product, vendor, procurement and expenses cost optimisation using advanced profitability models

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Manual collection of data - Basic product profitability analysis with limited visibly on direct and indirect costs – no vendor level  or cross vendor comparison -  Cost driven procurement – high level OPEX monitoring
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Semi automated data collection - Product profitability analysis without addressing root causes of cost increase -  Vendor profitability based on cost of sales only - Cost driven procurement – limited cost optimization initiatives . Typically standard ERP reporting at summary levels.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Timely and on demand  vendor and product  performance analysis with a granularity on the product level in an automated exception driven process – good understanding of vendor profitability - well defined pricing guidance – Cost optimization initiatives  in place lacking prioritization  - Enhanced procurement decisions limited to major products . Combination of ERP and non ERP data.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Clear cost of sales structure in place – Detailed product profitability analysis and well defined pricing structure – Cost efficient vendor negotiations and purchase agreement - consistent cost calculation methods across the enterprise and across vendors – Procurement policy taking into consideration implication on supply chain
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Cross Vendor and product cost analysis - Vendor portfolio management – Clear vendor/supplier mix in place -  Optimize  processes based  on cost implication - adherence to expense containment policies throughout the organization – Well prioritized OPEX reduction initiatives eliminating low value high cost activities

bacr_question_full: Global Spend Visibility - Consolidating and integrating purchase information from multiple source ERPs to provide a global view of spend information

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: No automated approach, manual collection of data at summarised level.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Fixed time frame, semi automated reporting at an aggregated level with limited visibility for “global” vendors.  Limited consolidation to “global” vendor or for cross region materials because of poor master data references.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing:
Timely and on demand  purchasing reports at location/sku granularity in an automated exception driven process.
Multiple currencies supported with consolidation to primary currency (e.g. USD) for reporting, use of DUNS or other global identifier for vendor hierarchies across regions.
Purchase Price variation analysis with alerts in place.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Use of risk management techniques to identify and reduce supply disruption.  Identification of supplier  and product risks at a global level.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Near time event driven alerts to support purchasing strategy (e.g. Oil purchase hedging or other commodities).

bacr_question_full: Purchasing Optimisation - Optimize costs to servce model by improving vendor terms and conditions balancing cost of inventory, handling and storage

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Manual collection of data - Basic product profitability analysis with limited visibly on direct and indirect costs –manual intuitive assessment of spot buy opportunities - Cost driven procurement
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Semi automated data collection - Product profitability analysis without addressing root causes of cost increase - limited cost optimization initiatives  related to inventory and storage cost  -  Manual assessment of spot buy opportunities with lack of proper forecasting capabilities.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Timely and on demand  procurement  cost analysis with a granularity on the product level in an automated exception driven process – good understanding of vendor profitability – Procurement Cost optimization initiatives  in place lacking prioritization  - Enhanced procurement decisions limited to major products - assessment of spot buy opportunities with ,limited manual forecasting capabilities.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Clear cost of sales structure in place – Detailed product profitability analysis and well defined pricing structure – Cost efficient purchase agreement  negotiations--  Procurement policy taking into consideration implication on supply chain – Automated and analytics driven forecasting capabilities
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Cross Vendor and product cost analysis -  Optimized  processes based  on cost implication - adherence to expense containment policies throughout the organization – purchasing optimization fully integrated with spend analytics capabilities

bacr_question_full: Supplier Risk Management - Proactively assess and balance supply across the supply base to mitigate potential risks to supply

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: No automated approach, manual collection of data at summarised level.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Fixed time frame, semi automated reporting at an aggregated level with limited visibility for vendors.    Generally performed after vendor issues have started to determine potential impact – very ad-hoc type of analysis
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Supplier Performance and trend early warning alerts, for sudden or long term changes based on delivery or quality types of changes.  Identification of “top” vendors, impact to COGS for price changes, some sensitivity analysis on pricing impact to COGS. Vendor stability analysis, evaluating external financial sources and other media to identify potential changes in a vendors ability to deliver (e.g. poor financial performance, potential mergers and sales, etc…)
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Identification of risks exposure to a vendor and product shortage based on forecasted demand  Tracking through of all finished goods relying on a particular vendor/material to support sales, link to product classification (Sole, Single, Commodity) to determine potential exposure to sales.   Price comparison including “total landed cost” of a material from one vendor or another, including all terms, currencies, taxes, inventory holding etc… to compare actual costs.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Rapid analysis of potential supply  disruption in the event of unplanned external influences (disaster, terrorism etc), understanding the potential impact on supply and identification of mitigating actions to protect supply and service.

bacr_question_full: Forecasting (Short/Long Term) - deliver the most accurate prediction of demand to improve supply chain performance

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging:
No automated approach, manual collection of data at summarised level. Typically a top down approach using averages
Short historical used (often 4 to 6 weeks), no reaction to trend, poor forecast accuracy (if measured)
maturity_descriptors.2_developing:
Fixed time frame, semi automated forecasting at an aggregated level with basic allocation of forecast across products and/or locations based upon heuristics.
Short term forecast horizon, poor forecast accuracy
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing:
Timely and on demand  forecasting  at location/sku granularity in an automated exception driven process
Multiple forecast methods applied automatically, self adapting to  trend, specific method for slow moving products.
Automatic seasonal profiling catering for short and long seasonal products. Forecasting over varying time horizons and time buckets (daily/weekly) – vastly improved forecast accuracy
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating:
Demand model analytics approach using multiple  internal and external influences (eg weather, price, competition)
Model forecast for new product and new stores. Advanced daily forecasting and reforecasting techniques
maturity_descriptors.5_leading:
Real time interpretation of social media, web interaction, customer sentiment, location based analytics
Near time event driven demand predictions.
Affinity and cannibalisation impact of promoted and non-promoted product
Within day on demand forecasting in hourly time buckets to support short lead time replenishment (12 hours)

bacr_question_full: Event Management - Delivering an end to end planning and management capability to improve promotion and seasonal event revenue and margin performance

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: No automated approach, manual collection of  historical data at summarised level, generally excel spreadheet to predict promotional uplifts and seasonal event sales. High level forecasts broken down to store level using average store contribution to product group sales. Limited analysis of promotional success (typically reporting impact on promoted items only). Poor forecast accuracy
maturity_descriptors.2_developing:
Promotional forecasts generated at product level using previous promotional performance of similar promotions. Uplifts broken down to location level using averages
Limited analysis of promotional success (typically reporting impact on promoted items only)
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing:
Promotional uplift forecasts and sales profiles generated for each location based on previous promotional performance  typically using simple price elasticity models and key causal factors (eg media type and quality)
Limited analysis of promotional success (typically reporting impact on promoted items and category performance), considering pull forward of demand. On-going analysis of promotion performance from day 1 of promotion,
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating:
Using past promotional performance and associated promotional mechanics to  create predictive models. Using association analysis to estimate cannibalisation/halo impact on other non promoted items. Identifying key item to drive larger baskets through promotion. Using a bottom up forecasting approach  with “what if” capabilities
Calendar adjustment regarding historical years
Measuring the full impact of the promotion (promoted item, associated items, categories, baskets, missions) v targets
maturity_descriptors.5_leading:
Real time interpretation of social media,, web interaction, customer sentiment, location based analytics
Near time event driven demand predictions.
Exception alerts to highlight poor and over performing locations and products . Prediction of end of promotion performance v targets.

bacr_question_full: Forecast Performance Managmeent - To nmeasure and improve the foreasting process to better support the supply chain planning and exectuion functions in a more economical fashion

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: No automated approach, manual collection and reporting of data, inconsistent use (method) of metrics, Typically measuring accuracy by product on a weekly or monthly basis, not considering accuracy by location or by smaller time buckets (ie not MAPE)
maturity_descriptors.2_developing:
Fixed time frame, semi automated reporting at an aggregated level  using MAPE with limited forecast “lags”*.   

* Lags are the horizon the forecast is made compared to the actual it is compared to – e.g. a 2 Month lag is a forecast made 2 months earlier for the current month comparison.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing:
Forecast performance measured at multiple levels, across multiple lags to support performance measures vs. various decision points (e.g. vendor contract time, production commit time, distribution time, etc…).  Evaluating the performance  (of forecasting) of advertising and promotional activities.
Multiple measures applied, consistent method of calculation across the organization.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating:
Use of different historical data types – invoice, shipment, order, … to determine best method for supporting supply chain decisions.  Impact analysis of forecast error – tying to inventory value,, COGS, production variability, expediting costs.
Production/Supply delays highlighted to remove from “error” components caused by supply constraints.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Bringing in Economic and external information to identify causes of forecast error and incorporate into the forecast process to improve the actual forecast.  Example is weather data or new housing starts etc… that impact product usage in the long or short term.

bacr_question_full: Order Analysis - Optimising the accuracy of orders and the effective flow of inventory

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Orders reviewed manually each day removing any time to model, tune and maintain ordering parameters which leads to additional inaccuracies in orders meaning even more orders are manually adjusted. Leads to “knee jerk” over-reactions  to either reduce inventory or reduce out of stocks in an on-going cycle. Many emergency orders raised out of the normal ordering cycle.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Orders continue to be reviewed manually every day. “Back to basics” exercise performed on an infrequent basis to review and adjust ordering parameters to reflect current business conditions and demand profiles. Improves order accuracy on a temporary basis but will become obsolete within time so benefits not sustained.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Orders automatically reviewed against targets (eg stock cover generated, potential out of stocks)  generating exception alerts to highlight potential issues allowing majority of orders within target to be released automatically without manual review allowing users to focus on order exceptions and the underlying reasons  and tune ordering parameters where appropriate.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Orders automatically reviewed against targets (eg stock cover generated, potential out of stocks)  generating exception alerts to highlight potential issues allowing majority of orders within target to be released automatically without manual review . System automatically identifies causes of exceptions and recommends adjustments
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Automated process for monitoring ordering parameters to remain within targets, highlighting potential ordering issues before they arise, providing the use with “what if” capability to model the optimum replenishment parameters going forward. Need a long term demand and inventory plan  detailing projected orders and deliveries to support the process.

bacr_question_full: Fulfilment - Deliver just in time inventory through the supply chain to meet customer demand at the best economical level

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: No automated approach, manual collection of data at summarised level, and order pushed manually using spreadsheets or rudimentary solutions on an as need basis, typically using min max replenishment calculations. Limited order accuracy analysis
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Fixed time frame, semi automated replenishment considering basic ordering constraints (MOQ, lead time, order cycle,) Manual management of constraints and safety stock,. High levels of manual intervention to review and release orders. High levels of stockouts and  high levels of inventory across stores and products, no consistency.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing:
Timely and on demand  replenishment at location/sku granularity in an automated exception driven process
Multiple replenishment methods applied automatically for push and pull replenishment.  Dynamic management of safety stock levels using contribution analysis of the performance of each item in each location.   Automatic release of orders reducing manual intervention. Significantly reduced out of stocks and inventory levels
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating:
Multiple source and echelon managed to replenish stores in the most efficient way, with ability to change flow very quickly in response to demand volatility.
Ability to react quickly to unforeseen events by tracking them and adjust order and replenishment which are already in the pipe
Time-phased future order plans  to support collaboration, strategic planning and capacity planning and what if planning
maturity_descriptors.5_leading:
Real time analysis of demand volatility to adjust order quantities.
Intra-day, on demand  order generation enabling rapid replenishment to support perishable products

bacr_question_full: Product Lifecycle Management - actively manage products through their lifecycles to ensure the most appropriate stocking and inventory management policies are applied at each lifecycle stage

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging:
Manual planning of product introduction and end of life using spreadsheets resulting in poor availability and excess inventory across locations
Manual adjustment of inventory factors (desired service, safety stock levels etc), typically left to the last minute of forgotten
maturity_descriptors.2_developing:
Tracking early product performance at chain level compared to  forecast, typically weekly, some stores sell out some stores have excess stock – manual process to rebalance stock
End of life managed manually, typically, demand shaping activities left until too late to clear residual stocks. Measures taken at chain level resulting in some stores selling out early and others still having residual stock
Automated mature replenishment  though typical F&R system to manage products through mature lifestage
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing:
Tracking early product  performance by location by day, to identify potential under and over stock situation allowing early reaction to ensure stock is optimally balanced across all locations
Use controlled end of life residual stock prediction and manual modelling of remedial actions to improve sell through and reduce residual stocks
Manual management of supply chain constraints through the lifecycle, typically reactive, not planned and proactive
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Automatically adjusting safety stock factors each week (desired service levels, forecast sensitivity, etc) based on product sales performance at each stage of its lifecycle. Availability maintained throughout lifecycle  and inventory automatically managed out of the supply chain when needed. Seasonal sales profiles automatically created and maintained
maturity_descriptors.5_leading:
Agile hold and flow techniques employed to ensure the right inventory goes to the right stores based on early life performance, integrated with allocation and replenishment solutions
End of life residual stock position automatically predicted  in each location with recommendations of remedial actions to ensure optimal sell through to drive margin and revenue

bacr_question_full: Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) - To evaluate and actively balance future demand and supply, to plan production, capacity, resources and inventory, linking to the business/financial plan

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: No automated approach, manual collection and reporting of data, inconsistent use (method) of metrics, arguing on where numbers come from/derived. Multiple versions of the same data resulting in inconsistencies. No formal S&OP process, data reviewed on an ad-hoc basis infrequently.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: More formal “Excel” based reporting process, single owner, more consistency of data, but still issues over synchronisation of data  extracts and granularity of data resulting in inaccurate KPIs. S&OP review process formalised with regular (weekly/monthly) review cycles
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Formal S&OP tool with drill down capability, documentation of assumptions, systematic approach to data source and integration.  Ability to do root cause and view Aggregate to detailed level of S&OP hierarchy for all products/services. Exception capability to highlight potential issues.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating:
Ability to do “what-if” analysis for supply constraints and to adjust plans and allocate product by profitability/key customers etc…
Financial components (e.g. reports in currency, not just quantity) being used to help drive decisions on demand/supply and profitability.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Brining in Economic and external information to identify/predict causes of demand and supply changes.  These are incorporated in the planning process to improve the plan as well as understand financial implications.  Example is weather data or new housing starts etc… that impact product usage in the long or short term.  Other examples include a hurricane that reduces product supply from a given region/port and will cause changes that impact inventory/supply/demand for a period of time.

bacr_question_full: Supply Network Optimisation - Optimise the Supply Chain Network by identifying the ideal locations for manufacturing facilities, warehouses, and /or distribution and fulfillment centers

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: No automated approach to determining locations of facilities or transportation lanes/provider.  Decisions are based upon minimal analysis of historical data intended to predict future requirements. Decisions made in isolation with no consideration of impacts on other operations or the wider supply chain.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Infrequent use of basic high level  information to occasionally review current network structure and make minor changes to improve flow of good through the supply chain. Data isn’t integrated therefore most decisions are made in isolation and don’t consider  wider supply chain implications
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Regular use of consolidated data to foster an on-going review of the current network structure.  Includes use of future projected volumes by regions and/or demographics to provide the ability to plan and recommend future changes. Majority of time is still spent on collecting and consolidating data from multiple systems.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating:
Creation of a single view of integrated , consistent supply chain data which drives regular  pre-emptive modification to transportation network design and/or providers as well as future projected requirements. Decisions consider the wider supply chain implications with the ability to model the impact of changes on the rest of the supply chain.
Use of on-line demand and delivery geo-spatial  data to plan on-line fulfilment modes and locations (eg service from DC, existing Store or fulfilment centre)
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Real time analysis of predicted demand used to dynamically change transportation requirement and drive facility optimization to react to potential demand changes across the network.

bacr_question_full: Distribution / Fulfillment Performance Analysis - Provide the ability to measure, predict and enhance the performance of distirbution and fulfillment activities

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Manual system of data entry and collection of internal and external data required to report performance metrics on a weekly or monthly  frequency. Typically based around each location, no overall visibility of performance.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Some integration with 3PL providers and internal data sources such that daily or weekly reporting of performance metrics is accomplished for most all operations within the supply chain. Inconsistent reporting of performance data across different locations.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Automated consolidation and integration of all data within the supply chain (both internal and external providers) enabling consistent daily reporting of all distribution, fulfilment and transportation functions to all operating personnel.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Near real time ability to report performance in all areas of the logistics execution service areas, providing visibility of potential bottlenecks allowing pre-emptive actions to mitigate impacts.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Real time ability to know report and predict performance in all areas of the logistics execution service areas (distirbuiton center, fulfilment operation and transportation).  This includes the ability to provide advanced notification to customers and trading partners of future expected delivery ETA as well as regular updates as required.

bacr_question_full: Lot / Batch Track and Trace - Provide the ability to quickly identify the history associated with products and components/ingredients to minimise impact and financial exposure

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Manual system of data entry and collection of supplier and manufacturing data.  Location specific, no overall visibility of data. No capability to trace causes or impacts of issues.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Some integration with suppliers and other partners in the supply chain to track component products/ingredients as well as movement of goods throughout the supply chain. Still no overall visibility of data. Limited capability to trace causes or impacts of issues
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Regular automated consolidation and  integration of all key manufacturing data to allow for a full view of products components as well as storage locations and point of sale (POS). Enables causal analysis and impact analysis of issues, with focussed recall activities
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Integrated data with both suppliers as well a retailers which ties lot/batch activity to consumer purchases at the point of purchase. Full visibility of product history allowing granular causal and impact analysis with highly focussed recall activities (Capability includes the ability to initiate rapid communication with will parties effected by impacted product)
maturity_descriptors.5_leading:
Real time ability to know the location of all lots and batches of a product, allowing immediate remedial actions (eg stopping production line, distribution etc)  This capability includes both internal and external locations, including consumer contact information (phone, address, etc).  
Analysis of historical issues and impacts to predict and pre-empt future issues.

bacr_question_full: Shipment / Load Planning - Improve supply chain cost effectiveness and service levels by optimizing the shipment and load planning process

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Ad-hoc, no automated approach, manual collection and interpretation of data to support consolidation of container loads of single sku / single vendor truck loads
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Time interval, No automated approach, manual collection and interpretation of data to support consolidation of multiple sku, single vendor truck loads
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Automated time interval,  rule based analysis of data to aggregate multiple sku per vendor using demand / order projections not only of next bulk order but also of future bulk orders for order pull forward
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating:
Active automated time interval, rule based container load suggestions based on multiple sku over multiple vendors  based on incoterms (eg. FOB consolidation per source mainport for far east container deliveries) for upcoming delivery using pull forward.
Modelling ordering, transport, distribution constraints to optimise container fill through demand shaping and joint replenishment processes
maturity_descriptors.5_leading:
Active automated time interval, rule based container load suggestions based on multiple sku over multiple vendors  based on incoterms (eg. FOB consolidation per source mainport for far east container deliveries).
Ability to perform “what  if” scenario analysis to determine the optimum way of executing the load

bacr_question_short: Availability / Lost Sales Analysis and Optimisation
bacr_question_full: Availability / Lost Sales Analysis and Optimisation - Improve product availability through the prediction and active management fo potential lost sales situations

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Manual, infrequent silo’d, summarised, measurement of on shelf availability, typically, spreadsheet based, using end of day inventory levels to calculate availability. Availability typically based on number of products in range which are out of stock (no consideration of volume)
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: More systematic reporting of on shelf availability using BI tool. Considers sales volume of each out of stock item to provide a demand weighted view  of availability, still based on end of day inventory and only considers full days of out of stock – typically inaccurate for slow moving products
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Causal analysis of poor availability with basic calculations of lost sales by comparing actual sales to forecast sales. Ability to track causes of lost sales back through the supply chain to identify opportunities to improve systemic issues (forecast accuracy, supplier performance, lead times etc)
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating:
Employing different probability modelling techniques for slow and fast moving products 
Using with in day sales to identify when  a product went off sale (before end of day) and when it came back on sale (after start of day) and calculate an accurate lost sales based upon a demand model
Using probability models to identify  potential out  of stock situations of slow moving giving a more accurate assessment
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Using near time sales to predict and identify  potential lost sales  of fast moving products and generate alerts to warn stores to check deliveries, back room stock to ensure product is available to sell.

bacr_question_short: Supply Chain Visibility - Provides the end to end
bacr_question_full: Supply Chain Visibility - Provides the end to end, time phase inventory visibilty by product and inventory status throughout the enterprise

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Manual system of data entry and collection of internal and external data required to track inventory and associated costs throughout the supply chain. Typically by location with little integration or visibility across the supply chain
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: integration of high level summarised data with 3PL providers and internal data sources such that a daily or weekly snapshot of inventory, orders, shipments and costs throughout the supply chain is available to the organization.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Regular automated consolidation and  integration of all detailed data within the supply chain (both internal and external providers) so that current and future inventory plans are available throughout the supply chain. Provides consistent data and reporting KPI’s across the supply chain
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Near real time ability to report inventory and costs in all areas of the supply chain, highlighting potential future inventory issues
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Real time visibility to inventory  and costs throughout the supply chain supporting supply chain planning and risk mitigation activities.  This includes the ability to provide detailed costs at the SKU level and rolled up at facility and/or customer views.

bacr_question_short: Order to Cash - Link Sales and Finance organisations
bacr_question_full: Order to Cash - Link Sales and Finance organisations, integrating sales with customer payments, returns, rebates etc to help determine true customer profitability

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: No automated approach, manual collection and reporting of data.  Long latency on reporting and collection activities.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: ERP supported reporting of sales and receivables data.  Timely, but limited to ERP capabilities, manual effort for identifying mismatches between terms, payments, prices, etc…
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Consolidated Receivables  information  and reports, on demand, by product,  customer, region, organization etc…  Alerts or rankings by payments not matching deliverables, currency conversion differences and other miss-matches between terms, conditions, expected and actual receivables.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Balancing (optimizing) between terms, payments and price with customers to ensure on time payment, but considering all aspects of the total profitability of the goods.  Actions that support reduction of Days Sales Outstanding and cash collections.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Integrating ERP and ERP information at the most granular level to provide a definitive view of cash flow and accurate allocations of costs. Proactive monitoring of cash flow highlighting potential issues and challenges through exceptions  and alerts

bacr_question_full: Supply Chain Financial Performance Analysis - Drive better business decisions based on financial impacts and performance of the supply chain

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Manual, infrequent silo’d, summarised, measurement of basic supply chain performance , spreadsheet based. No consistency across locations.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Measure standard supply chain metrics (CPC, Labour rates, pick rates etc) using averages, weekly/monthly, semi-automated data capture and analysis. Still oriented to each location, no overall supply chain view.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Automated consolidation and integration of supply transactions and costs across all locations in the supply chain allowing key operational processes to be aligned to financial performance. Consistent reporting across the supply chain with exception analysis highlighting best/poor performing processes/locations.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating:
Ability to capture, allocate and provide full visibility of all detailed cost through the supply chain to develop a detailed cost and profitability model by product, location and Customer at any point in time
Build profitability models over product lifetime. Build detailed cost to serve models to identify opportunities to drive efficiencies.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Near real time simulation and what if impact analysis of changes to supply chain to support supply chain optimisation

bacr_question_full: Quality Management - Provide an overall view across the entire value chain and life cycle to support consistent metrics, drive best pracitces and improve yield and customer satisfaction

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: No automated approach, manual collection of data at summarised level. Segregated non-consistent approach
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Semi automated KPIs calculation on transactional data or available ERP data. Collection and integration of data  usually in Excel or other limited access tools
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Integrated bottom up and top down view of company wide shared KPIs on manufacturing quality. Automated collection of data and display though dashboards and standardized reports
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Integrated bottom up and top down transparency  of quality KPIs expanded with discovery capabilities to search for and detect emerging quality issues
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Real time KPI calculation based on data collected across the entire manufacturing process and life cycle.  External data (e.g. weather, AT) and other factors to relate to production quality/yield.  Sensor data analysis to determine quality of the actual sensors.

bacr_question_full: Manufacturing Performance - Improve the supply (production) capabilities of the manufacturing organisation in the most economical fashion

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: No automated approach, manual collection and reporting of data.  Long latency on reporting and collection activities.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Siloes of reporting within and across sites.  Metrics are provided, but  little consistency in method and process.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Site and “global” level consistent metrics, integrating ERP, MES, Quality, MRO etc… manufacturing data.  Root cause analysis supported on a timely basis with automated collection of data.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Sensor data analysed and alerts with business rules recommend process deviation.  KPI’s across plants are provided to improve individual plant performance.  Predictive maintenance techniques in place to reduce un-planned down time of equipment.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Real time capture of sensor data from the factory floor, with alerts and triggers to signal quality/performance deviation and recommend changes,  Parameter management in place to signal changes in data being used in planning and control systems (e.g. lead time deviation),

bacr_question_full: Global Plant Visibility - Provide an overall view across all plants / facilities to support consistent metrics, drive best practices and improve yield

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: No automated approach, manual collection of data at summarised level.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Semi automated KPIs calculation by plant, usually in Excel or other limited access tools
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Automatic data collected for each of the plants individual systems with KPI calculations, summarized view across plants on a scheduled basis (usually monthly), but inconsistent metrics calculations
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Global activity monitoring across facilities and process, integration of plant  (MES, QM, MRO, Historian, Sensor) and ERP systems.  Condition Based Maintenance and root cause supported.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Real time KPI calculation based on data collected across all plants.  External data (e.g. weather, AT) and other factors to relate to production quality/yield.  Sensor data analysis to determine quality of the actual sensors.

bacr_question_full: Fleet Management - Locate, manage and optimise fleet investments aligned with business strategy

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Manual system and processes for tracking fleet inventory and costs across some or all of the supply chain network.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Some integration within the organization to automate the location and utilization of the fleet.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: The ability to track the location and full utilization of all of the fleet within an organization.  This includes the ability to identify most operating and depreciation costs.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Near real time tracking of the location and utilization of the fleet.  The ability to track all operating costs down to the individual unit within the fleet.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Real time visibility to all units within the fleet.  This level includes the ability to predict future utilization as well as anticipated operational costs down to the unit level.

bacr_question_full: Logistics Capacity Analysis - take long range plans and forecasts to create a roadmap required to ensure capacity for future growth exists

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: No automated approach to determining locations of facilities or transportation lanes/provider.  Decisions are based upon minimal analysis of historical data intended to predict future requirements.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Use of basic information to occasionally review current capacities and make minor changes to improve flow of good through the supply chain. Decisions taken in isolation, not considering impacts on other supply chain processes or facilities.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Regular analysis of  consolidated data to foster an on-going review of the current logistics capacities.  Includes some use of future projected volumes by regions and/or demographics.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Integrated supply chain data providing a single supply chain view. Regular modification to facility locations and sizes, processing areas to reflect future demand and capacity requirements,  transportation fleets and/or 3rd party providers. Exception reporting to predict and highlight potential capacity issues. “what –if” capability to determine impacts of changes to supply chain operations on the rest of the supply chain.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Real time analysis of predicted demand used to dynamically change logistics resources as required to maintain capacities at manageable levels and maintain supply chain service.

bacr_question_full: Logistics Efficiency Analysis -Analysis to ensure that the best logistics service is being provided at the most economical cost

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Manual, infrequent silo’d, summarised, measurement of basic Logistics performance, spreadsheet based. No consistency across facilities
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Measure standard Logistics metrics (OTIF, pick rates, vehicle fill etc) weekly/monthly, semi-automated data capture and analysis by location/facility. No end to end visibility across the supply chain
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing:
Single integrated, consistent view of detailed supply chain performance data allowing comparisons of facilities performance 
On demand automated measurement of key logistics metrics and dashboards 
Assigning actual costs to detailed performance metrics to identify cost saving and efficiency opportunities
Timely evaluation of historical lane, mode , 3PL usage metrics
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Ability to capture, and provide full visibility of all Logistics performance metric and link to end Customer service achievement  identifying causes of service failures and identification of service improvement opportunities
maturity_descriptors.5_leading:
Real time visibility of logistics performance  used to make inflight changes  to manage risk from unplanned events and maintain service (eg flood in a DC redirect orders to other DC, expedite decision (fly v ship))

Prediction of future performance challenges based on analysis of historical performance allowing pre-emptive actions to alleviate or mitigate impacts and maintain service

bacr_question_full: Freight / Carrier Analysis - The economic measurement of transportation costs and performance as a component of the cost of goods sold

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Manual system and processes for tracking shipment cost and delivery performance across some or all of the supply chain network.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Some integration with 3PL providers and internal data sources in order to provide weekly or monthly freight performance measurement.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Regular batch integration of all freight data within the supply chain (both internal and external providers) so that daily performance reporting is available throughout the supply chain.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Near real time freight performance tracking and cost reporting.  This includes the ability to identify network improvement including carrier routing and lane modifications.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Real time visibility to internal freight and carrier performance throughout the supply chain.  This includes cost performance, service level tracking and the ability to identify real time routing and lane modifications to improve overall performance.
